#4943. Bitcoin returns to 200-week trend line as analyst sees risk of $57.7K next

Bitcoin price action interacted with its 200-week simple moving average for the first time since mid-August as it fell below $68,000.

Bitcoin (BTC) fell to $67,500 on Friday, slipping below its 200-week simple moving average on its first test of the level in nearly three months.

TradingView data showed that Bitcoin last touched its 200-week simple moving average (SMA) on Aug. 19.

BTC/USD one-day chart with the 200-week SMA. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

The 200-week SMA has served as a reference point for Bitcoin’s cycle lows, acting as support or resistance during bear markets. Bitcoin traded around the average from March to October 2023 and again from June to mid-August this year. Decisive moves back above it on the weekly chart have preceded sharper rallies.

In his latest analysis, Keith Alan, cofounder of crypto trading platform Material Indicators, flagged the 200-week SMA as having confluence with a resistance/support flip level on Bitcoin’s relative strength index (RSI).

Weekly RSI has returned to 41.5, a level that it established as support in late July after it spent several weeks attempting a breakout.

“Losing 41.5 on Weekly RSI opens the door to test the cycle low at $57.7k,” Alan wrote Friday on X, noting the bullish implications that successfully defending the support zone would have.

BTC/USD one-week chart with 200 SMA; RSI data. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

BTC price downside accelerated on Friday as Asia markets reacted to the resignation and ongoing controversy around Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Hong Kong’s Hang Seng finished the day down 1.55%, while South Korea’s KOSPI Composite Index ended 0.98% lower.

Related: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO, exits board; shares plunge

US stock-market futures fell slightly, with the Nasdaq 100 falling 0.2% as analysis eyed a redistribution of capital into Nvidia’s competitors, preserving the AI trade.

Nasdaq 100 futures one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

“What you’re seeing in markets now is a bit of a rotation into other advanced chip design companies, on the assumption that this will enable other companies effectively to catch up,” said Mark Franklin, head of multi-asset solutions for Asia at asset manager Manulife Investment Management, told CNBC.

Nvidia stock was 0.7% higher pre-market, meanwhile, amid reports of growing support for Huang’s return. An internal post quoted by Wired drew more than 1,600 comments from employees.

Nvidia futures one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

The Goop Guide is indeed recorded inside a studio, but Paltrow approached the space with just as much intention as her own home, enlisting interior designer Marie Carson to bring it to life. “I wanted it to feel like a beautiful, elevated nook of somebody’s old stone house somewhere,” Paltrow tells AD of the space.

The catch? Carson only had mere days to turn the sterile studio into something far cozier and conducive to the wide-ranging conversations Paltrow hoped to conduct during the show, which launches with Zoe Saldana as the first guest. “We started to decorate remotely and I looked at it and thought, This is not the direction,” Paltrow says of the space’s first iteration. “And so I called Marie and said, ‘We’re filming in, like, a week and I need you to come and fix this.’”

It wasn’t the tight timeline that initially gave Carson pause. “At first I said, ‘Oh my gosh, I’ve never done a set! What does that mean?’” recalls the designer. “But when Gwyneth said she wanted it to feel like a beautiful room in her home, I thought, Well, I can do that.” Previously, the two had collaborated on a space at Paltrow’s Brentwood property, which meant there was already a creative shorthand between them—incredibly helpful when they had only days to outfit the space before shooting commenced. “Gwyneth has such a strong direction of what she wants and such excellent taste,” Carson says. “So I was able to take her notes and run with it.”

The focal point for the studio’s design is a late-18th-century Flemish tapestry. “It added life to the space,” says Carson.

The Goop Kitchen founder wanted the focal point of the design to be a late-18th-century Flemish tapestry, whose landscape imagery features a palette of muted greens and taupes. “I thought it would be beautiful because of what they’ve lived through and what they’ve seen,” Paltrow says of tapestries. “I love them because you think about all the life going on in front of these things for hundreds and hundreds of years.” To complement the hanging, Carson added a 19th-century Belgian trestle table from Meg Turner Gallery, antique chairs reupholstered in Loro Piana brushed cashmere, and a handwoven hemp and silk rug sourced from Mansour. “Marie’s execution is flawless,” Paltrow says. “She has a real knack for finding the perfect thing that has the right dimensions and warmth.”

Paltrow commissioned a painting of magnolia from artist Rob Reynolds. The sconces are from Goop’s collection with CB2 and the wicker stools are from Galerie Provenence.

A close-up of one of the podcast chairs: an antique sourced from a shop in Pasadena and reupholstered with Loro Piana cashmere.

In the handful of shows Paltrow’s filmed so far, it appears her guests (which include Rick Rubin, Ke Huy Quan, and more) feel similarly at home. “Everyone who walks in is like, ‘I’ve done so many podcasts and I’ve never seen one like this! It feels like a real room and I feel so at ease.’’’ she says. Considering Paltrow will be filming dozens of episodes inside the space, she’s happy it’s comfortable for her as well. “I would definitely live in this room,” she says. “I think about this room all the time now when I’m not in it because I’m so obsessed with it.”

#4939. The 7 Best Garmin Watches, Tested by Our Fitness and Tech Experts

Garmin has a watch for every type of athlete and budget.

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

Brands like Whoop, OURA, and Apple offer some of the best fitness trackers available, but Garmin watches remain the go-to for serious athletes and outdoor enthusiasts. Men’s Health editors have trusted these wearables to go the distance during ultramarathons, multi-day hikes, and backcountry ski trips thanks to their weeks-long battery life and pinpoint GPS accuracy. But they’re equally useful for everyday life and weekend warriors—we love wearing the Garmin Approach S70 for golf rounds because it comes preloaded with more than 43,000 courses from around the world.

The current Garmin lineup is more robust than ever, from entry-level running watches to premium expedition-ready models that cost upwards of $1,000. Several models come with full-color topographic maps, military-grade durability, and hardcore activity-specific metrics. For instance, runners get detailed stride analysis, cyclists receive power metrics, and swimmers enjoy stroke detection. They also offer specialized outdoor capabilities, including barometric altimeters for precise elevation tracking, compass sensors for navigation without GPS, and pulse oximeters that help monitor your acclimation at high altitudes.

The Garmin Vivoactive 6 offers health monitoring features like sleep coaching, recovery time recommendations, and training readiness scores. Meanwhile, adventure-focused models like the Garmin Instinct 3 and Garmin Fenix 8 Pro incorporate multi-band GPS for accuracy in dense forests, plus emergency features like fall detection and SOS alerts. Whether you’re tracking your first 5K or planning a summit attempt on a remote peak, there’s a Garmin designed specifically for your needs. We’ve logged thousands of miles testing these watches to help you find the perfect match.

Over the years, our editors have done it all: ultramarathons, multi-day backpacking trips, open water swims, and mountain expeditions. Through our adventures, Garmin watches have consistently proven their worth on our wrists. To find the best Garmin watches, we evaluated several models across multiple activities, testing their GPS accuracy, battery performance, and usability. We also considered factors like comfort during prolonged wear and durability when subjected to the elements. This testing allowed us to see how each watch performs out in the real world beyond the spec sheet.

The Fenix 8 stands as Garmin’s ultimate performance watch, offering detailed training insights and reliability for marathoners, ultra-runners, and multi-sport competitors. The watch doesn’t doesn’t track your runs—it analyzes every aspect of your performance with features like training readiness, recovery time, and PacePro technology, allowing you to plan your race-day strategy with GPS-based pace guidance. These features can help you optimize your performance.

Battery life remains exceptional even during GPS-intensive activities. While the standard 51mm AMOLED version delivers approximately 29 days, the solar-equipped model extends this to 48 days with adequate sun exposure. The watch offers multiple power management profiles that let you customize battery usage based on what you have planned that day. This ensures you have the data you need from start to finish without worrying about mid-race charging.

Beyond its training capabilities, the Fenix 8 serves as a reliable navigation tool during unfamiliar routes and trail races. The full-color topographic maps, turn-by-turn directions, and ClimbPro feature help you strategize your effort on challenging courses. You also get comprehensive recovery features, with detailed sleep tracking, HRV status, and body battery energy monitoring that help prevent overtraining.

While the Fenix 8’s price places it among the most expensive sport watches available (especially for the new Fenix 8 Pro), serious athletes who spend hundreds of hours training for major events will find the watch’s performance insights and bulletproof reliability well worth the investment. "This watch has everything that Garmin has to offer into a low-profile casing," says MH Fitness and Commerce Editor Charles Thorp, NASM. "Rugged enough to perform in tough terrain, but sleek enough to fit in everywhere else."

The Vivoactive 6 is one of Garmin’s more lifestyle-oriented models, offering a balance between everyday smartwatch functionality and robust fitness tracking. With its sleek design and comprehensive tracking features, it’s a solid alternative to the Apple Watch SE for those who want longer battery life (up to 11 days) and more comprehensive fitness metrics.

Through running and strength training sessions, the Vivoactive 6 offers detailed metrics about VO2 max, aerobic and anaerobic output, and exercise load. These insights provide a clearer picture of fitness progress than basic calorie and distance tracking. The responsiveness during workouts particularly stood out during our side-by-side comparison with the Apple Watch SE. When increasing running pace, the Vivoactive 6 updated immediately, while the Apple Watch lagged noticeably behind. During strength training, we appreciated the live heart rate zone updates, making it easier to gauge workout intensity in real time.

The most significant advantage over the Apple Watch is battery life. While our SE required daily charging, the Vivoactive 6 kept going for days between charges—a game-changer for active users. The comfortable fit works well even on smaller wrists, and at $299, it offers more fitness functionality than similarly priced competitors while maintaining everyday usability. It supports contactless payments and can even store music from your favorite Spotify playlists. If you want comprehensive fitness insights without the premium price, the Vivoactive 6 hits the sweet spot.

The Forerunner 970 is Garmin’s new flagship running watch, built for athletes who want every data point without sacrificing everyday usability. It pairs a brighter 1.4-inch AMOLED display with a built-in speaker and microphone, plus a tougher sapphire lens and lightweight titanium bezel, so it feels premium yet rugged enough for hard training.

During intervals and long runs, the interface is intuitive—pace, heart rate, and distance are all visible at a glance, and after each session the watch prompts you to rate how the run felt. The 970 also offers deeper performance tools, including running economy, running tolerance (when paired with Garmin’s HRM 600 chest strap), hill score, endurance score, and more detailed load analysis to show how hard you’re pushing week to week.

Battery life remains a major selling point. Garmin claims up to 15 days in smartwatch mode and 26 hours in GPS mode with multi-band SATIQ, so you can stack long runs, races, and daily training without worrying about charging. Built-in full-color maps, turn-by-turn directions, dynamic round-trip routing, ClimbPro, and Up Ahead make the watch just as useful on unfamiliar trails as it is for neighborhood miles.

Recovery and health tracking also see significant upgrades over older Forerunners. Training Readiness delivers a simple morning score based on recent sleep and workload, so you know whether to push or back off. Upgraded sleep tracking, nap detection, and newer tools like ECG readings also provide a clearer picture of how your body handles stress, illness, and heavy training weeks.

If you’re looking for something that’s durable, look no further than the Instinct 3. The watch offers military-grade construction that can withstand some real punishment, with a rugged design that proved its worth throughout testing. We accidentally banged it against doorways and scraped it against kettlebells during workouts, yet it emerged without a scratch. The distinctly masculine aesthetic features a substantial case housing an impressive array of sensors while maintaining water resistance to 100 meters.

Battery performance is one of the Instinct 3’s most impressive features. While Garmin claims 18 days between charges, our testing revealed closer to 21 days of regular use without heavy reliance on battery-intensive features. It makes it one of the longest-lasting watches in Garmin’s lineup, while providing a significant advantage over other mainstream smartwatches. When you do need a recharge, a quick 10-minute session can add several hours of use—perfect for those who forgot to charge before heading out the door.

For trail runs and hikers, the watch includes a digital compass that shows your precise directional heading, multi-band GPS with SatIQ technology, and a built-in flashlight with multiple intensity levels including a red light option. The Instinct 3 also features ABC sensors that provide real-time environmental data. Of course, the watch also offers powerful health and fitness features, including HRV status, stress tracking, and the ability to track your blood oxygen levels.

Read more: Our Garmin Instinct 3 AMOLED Review

Don’t let the lower price tag fool you: The Forerunner 165 packs serious running tech into a $249 package, making it the ideal option for runners who are just getting started on their journey or those looking to dip their toes into fitness trackers. This relative newcomer to Garmin’s lineup boasts an AMOLED display, a lightweight design, and advanced training metrics runners will appreciate.

Despite being positioned as an entry-level running watch, the Forerunner 165 outclasses similarly priced competitors with its premium build quality and thoughtful design. It’s incredibly comfortable, especially compared to Garmin’s bulkier models, while still maintaining the brand’s impressive durability. The AMOLED screen offers excellent readability even in bright sunlight, and text looks crisp. We particularly appreciated the intuitive physical button navigation combined with touchscreen functionality.

For runners who want their first serious training companion, the Forerunner 165 hits the sweet spot by delivering Garmin’s core running analytics without overwhelming users. While it lacks some of the advanced recovery tools found in the Forerunner 965 like Training Readiness, it covers all the essentials with accurate GPS tracking and guided workouts.

The Venu 4 is Garmin’s latest lifestyle smartwatch, and it feels like a smarter, more polished upgrade from the Venu 3. Available in 41mm and 45mm sizes, it pairs a bright AMOLED display with a metal case and a low-profile design for a clean, casual look that looks great both at the office and at the gym.

In testing, the Venu line has always stood out for being easy to live with, and the latest model doubles down on that. Battery life stretches up to roughly 12 days in smartwatch mode depending on how often you’re working out and using the always-on display, which means you don’t have to baby it with nightly charges—topping it up during a shower a few times a week is usually enough. The built-in LED flashlight is also a welcome addition for running at dusk or dawn, helping you stay visible to drivers. You also get a speaker and mic for taking calls and using your phone’s voice assistant from your wrist.

What makes the Venu 4 more than a standard smartwatch is that it treats your health as more than just steps and heart rate. Health status and lifestyle logging show how daily choices—like drinking caffeine later in the day—actually affect your sleep, stress, and heart rate variability, so the data feels more useful than just a bunch of charts. The Venu 4 also has the new Garmin Coach feature, with over 80 preloaded GPS and indoor sports apps that cover everything from walking and HIIT to yoga and strength training.

Its app and ecosystem integration still isn’t as far-reaching as an Apple Watch, especially on iPhone, but if you care more about deeper health tracking and better workouts, the Venu 4 is a great alternative that offers multi-day battery life and more recovery-focused insights.

The Approach S70 is the ultimate golf companion, delivering comprehensive course coverage—with over 43,000 preloaded courses worldwide—in a sleek, lightweight design. Available in two sizes (42mm and 47mm), this premium golf watch displays detailed course maps showing precise distance to greens, hazards, and doglegs, while the Virtual Caddie feature provides club recommendations based on your playing history and current conditions.

What truly sets the S70 apart is its attention to golf-specific details. The watch provides front, center, and back distance readings to every green, along with precise yardages to hazards. This is extremely helpful as sometimes you can’t even fully see a hole and have no idea that a water hazard is lying within distance of your next shot, so that overview of the hole is crucial info to have. The "plays like" feature accounts for elevation changes and wind when calculating distances, something that can be difficult to gauge on your own.

Beyond the thousands of preloaded courses, the S70 also displays green contour data to improve your putting strategy (Garmin Golf membership required). During our testing, the functions and how to navigate them took a little getting used to, but once we got that down, it was pretty easy after every shot just to twist our wrist to get our next distance. The AMOLED display has also been crisp and never difficult to see out in the sun.

At $699, the S70 is a significant investment, but for golfers who regularly play and want and easy way to gauge the shots to hit, the combination of golf-specific features and modern smartwatch functionality makes it a great companion on the course.

Read More: Our Review of the Garmin Approach S70

Depending on the Garmin you choose, you can expect battery life to last anywhere from a few days to a few weeks. The Fenix 8 AMOLED’s battery can stretch for up to 16 days, while the Fenix 8 with solar will go up to 21 days (28 days with solar). Of course, real-world battery performance can vary based on how you actually use your watch. Running a marathon with continuous GPS tracking? You’ll drain the battery much faster than if you’re just checking notifications and tracking daily steps.

Garmin has a reputation for offering several advanced training and recovery metrics, which can help you understand how ready your body is for exercise and optimize your training schedule. The Forerunner 970 offers Training Readiness, which synthesizes your sleep score, recovery time, acute training load, sleep history, and more to show "when you are most likely to benefit from a hard workout and when to consider dialing down to let your body catch up," Garmin says.Even if you don’t train every day, you can still benefit from Garmin’s more basic tracking features, like daily step count, calories, and sleep. Some models can even track your stress, monitoring your body’s physiological responses throughout the day. During a hectic workday or high-pressure meeting, knowing when you’re stressed can prompt you to take action—i.e., perform breathing exercises—which can make a difference in your overall well-being.Additionally, Garmin’s various models analyze detailed performance metrics to determine if your training is productive, offer built-in coaching features to prepare you for races, and suggest workouts tailored to your fitness level and goals. What makes Garmin’s approach so good is its flexibility—serious athletes can drive into the data, while casual users can stick with simpler metrics and guided programs.

GPS and Garmin go hand in hand, so it’s no surprise that the brand’s watches offer robust tracking and navigation. These features can be essential for runners, hikers, and outdoor athletes. Most Garmin watches provide detailed maps, turn-by-turn directions, and breadcrumb trails that help you retrace your steps. Some high-end models, like the aforementioned Fenix 8, offers offline maps with enhanced satellite imagery, SATIQ technology, ABC sensors, and more. These features can be invaluable for precise tracking even in steep valleys, offer reliable compass headings, and deliver accurate elevation readings.

Garmin watches traditionally prioritize function over fashion, packing them with a lot of tech and large batteries. As a result, they generally skew larger compared to many competitors. Some models come in multiple sizes—the Venu 4 is available with screen sizes of 41mm and 45mm, similar to the Apple Watch Series 11, which comes in 42mm and 46mm. However, the Venu 3 is still noticeably larger; it boasts a width of 45mm and a thickness of 12mm (compared to the Series 10’s 36mm and 9.7mm). That said, some of Garmin’s watches, like the Forerunner 970, only come in one size. If you have smaller wrists like I do, you have two options: Buy your preferred model and accept that it might look oversized on your wrist, or opt for one of Garmin’s more lifestyle-oriented models like the Vivoactive 6, which is 10.9mm thick. Garmin does offer "S" variants of several models specifically designed for small wrists—the Venu 3S, for example, is thinner and lighter than the normal Venu 3. However, these S models typically sacrifice battery life for their smaller footprint, so you’ll have to consider if that’s a compromise you’re willing to make.

There are a lot of Garmin watches to choose from—the brand lists five major lineups on its website. The Forerunner 165 is one of Garmin's most affordable models at $249, providing you essential training metrics, built-in GPS, and up to 11 days of battery life. The more full-featured Venu 4 jumps up in price to $549, offering more detailed health insights, better battery life, and a larger, more vibrant display. Garmin’s premium adventure watches command the highest prices, with the Fenix 8 starting at $899 and climbing to $1,099 for solar-equipped models with sapphire crystal displays. When deciding which Garmin is right for you, consider what features you truly need versus what’s nice to have. If you’re a casual runner, you might be best served by something in the Forerunner lineup. But if you regularly go hiking in the backcountry, you might find the premium price of a Fenix justified by its comprehensive navigation tools and extended battery life.

#4937. The 8 Best Workout Shorts for Women of 2026, Tested By Editors and Stylists

Our favorite pair is from, believe it or not, Amazon.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

I’ll be honest—working out in shorts was never really my thing. I’ve always been more of a leggings girl. I used to think flowy shorts felt too exposed and compression shorts weren’t flattering. But since I'm a style writer who lives a pretty active lifestyle, I figured it was time to give athletic shorts a real shot. Now, after testing over 20 pairs of workout shorts over the past almost two-and-a-half years, I can officially say I’m a convert.

Alongside stylists and other WH editors, I tested the internet's most popular workout shorts. Over the past two years, we evaluated them based on coverage, moisture-wicking abilities, comfort, size range, and fit. The result? A list of six fantastic pairs that we recommend for all types of workouts, including running, HIIT training, yoga, Pilates, and more.

I’ve tested a wide range of athletic shorts, but the Gym People High Waist Short topped my list for a few reasons: it’s super soft, has nice compression, comes in a ton of colors, and has many different pockets to store your belongings. Plus, said pockets don’t add any bulk to your legs—a rare find in a short.

My biggest pet peeve with athletic shorts is when they feel way too tight and restrictive. But this pair, made from a polyester-spandex blend, has four-way stretch that makes it feel breathable, light, and easy to move in. “The fit is a bit more compressive around the stomach, which gives a nice smoothing and lifting effect—something I actually appreciate since super stretchy biker shorts can sometimes feel a little shapeless around the hips,” says style contributor Lily Wohlner.While this short does offer some compression, it leans more on the stretchy side than super form-fitting, so it might not be the best pick for high-impact workouts. It feels supportive, but I wouldn’t wear it for running or burpees since it doesn’t hold me in quite enough. That said, the fabric is buttery soft—like, ridiculously comfortable—so it’s perfect for walking, yoga, and Pilates. I also love that it’s not see-through, so I felt totally fine stretching and bending without worrying. The only downside? The moisture-wicking could be better. Wohlner says she wore it to hot yoga once, and the sweat stains were definitely noticeable.Read More: Best Leggings For Working Out

So many WH editors love this short from lululemon, especially for running. "I hadn't bought a pair of running shorts in years, but given that I've taken up running as a hobby, I knew I needed some for moving in hot weather," says associate health & fitness editor Addison Aloian. This extremely lightweight short, made from polyester and elastane, stood out to her because it's light and airy and comes in a ton of colors. Plus, there's a little side pocket where you can store your keys while logging miles.

Fast forward to today—she has logged hundreds of miles in this short and says it’s her all-time favorite pair for hitting the pavement. But, she also loves its versatility because she can wear it paired with a big sweatshirt for running errands, to a yoga class, or during her weekly strength training sessions. It never chafes or rubs against her legs, even when things start to get sweaty. Plus, she says the four-inch inseam offers excellent coverage so her cheeks are fully covered while she’s out and about. “They never ride up or move around, which is hard to find in a running short,” she says.

Stylist Rose Lauture is also a mega fan of this short, but she actually prefers the shorter, 2.5-inch inseam option—it’s the shortest option on this list—for its super airy feel. Despite the shorter inseam, she never feels exposed, but opt for the longer pair if you want to feel more covered. However, both shorts have a built-in panty liner for added coverage, so you never have to worry about anything slipping out (IYKYK).Both testers commented on how quickly this short dries. After a run, Aloian says there were some sweaty spots, but they were completely dry by the time she was ready to shower.

When I reach for a flowy workout short, it’s usually this pair from Beyond Yoga. I’ve been wearing it a ton to heated Pilates classes (my latest hyperfixation), and the lightweight breathability is unmatched. It’s made from a lightweight, woven fabric comprised of polyester and elastane. Woven fabrics, as opposed to knit fabrics, tend to be super breathable—and the vented back panel and perforated material at the sides give this short an extra airy feel. I never overheat while wearing it, whether I’m sweating it out on the mat or running miles.

Speaking of, this short is the epitome of versatile—I love it for strength training when paired with the Spacedye Slim Tank (my #1 workout top!), but it’s also a great running short. Despite the non-stretch material, the waistband offers plenty of give (and is adjustable!) and the leg openings are wide enough to keep things comfortable without chafing or riding up at the inner thighs—IYKYK.

It’s also really flattering, especially for a short that lacks compression. The body-skimming, flowy silhouette somehow makes my lower belly look super snatched. I love wearing it for regular days running errands, paired with a matching tank or zip-up sweatshirt. My only small complaint is that I wish it were available in more core colors. Right now, you can get it year-round in two shades, but there are usually lots of fun seasonal options depending on when you’re browsing.

Read More: Beyond Yoga Spacedye Slim Cropped Tank Review

Have you seen a cuter pair of workout shorts? I love the retro design with colorblocking and contrasting trims along with the mesh panels at the sides and hem. It’s one of the few workout shorts I wear just as frequently outside of the gym as I do to break a sweat. Pair it with a simple white tank (or top in any other color featured in the short) and flip-flops, and you have the perfect vintage activewear fit. On colder outings, throw your favorite sporty hoodie on top for a good complement.

I’m also a big fan of the length: The approximately 5-inch inseam and roomy leg openings with notched hems at the sides give a leg-slimming effect and are also just super comfortable. It also makes sure I don’t accidentally show too much skin while running in my neighborhood or picking up weights at the gym. An added layer of protection there is the built-in brief, which, unlike many I’ve encountered, doesn’t feel like it's giving me a constant wedgie (I’ve literally cut them out of my shorts before, but I barely notice it in this short).

Another bonus? The mesh paneling I mentioned earlier is as stylish as it is breathable. Even when I throw it on for a run on a treadmill in a stuffy gym, things stay feeling light and airy.

I only wish this short came in more colors—I would genuinely purchase them all. Right now, you can snag it in two color combos, but I’d love to see a few more and maybe even a neutral option.

If you're looking for a buttery-soft workout fit, this biker short from Beyond Yoga is your best friend. The brand itself is a favorite among our fashion team, and that's because the fabrics, which are made from super soft polyester and elastane, are never tight and constricting, always smooth and soft (yet still contouring and flattering!).

Yes, the short is awesome for all sorts of workouts, but we also love it for running errands and, dare we say it, lounging, as it looks so cute with every outfit and feels so comfortable for all-day wear. Plus, it's moisture-wicking during sweaty workouts. Speaking of sunny days, the short also has built-in UV protection, because we're all about staying protected from the sun here.

The Spacedye Biker Short is also one of the longest options on this list, so it's a solid choice if you're looking for something with a bit more leg coverage.

I often wear this short to yoga, but it's compressive enough that it doesn't budge when I wear it for a run or to higher-intensity classes. According to stylist Kristen Saladino, the high-waisted fit makes you feel super tucked-in and secure without feeling constricted. And, if you need a larger size, this short goes all the way up to a 4XL.

I do wish there were more colors to choose from. As of now, the brand only offers two core colors in this short.

Sure, we love the lululemon short for running, but the Norvan Short from Arc'teryx is built for the trails—and that’s exactly what we use it for. Lauture gives this fitted short a big thumbs-up for feeling super light and breathable, especially on long runs. It’s made from 100% polyester, so it’s airy and helps keep you cool by letting moisture escape and regulating your body temp. And if things do get sweaty, the built-in moisture-wicking brief (with antimicrobial treatment) helps manage odor—so you don’t have to stress.

Got loose keys or headphones? There's a discreet zippered back pocket that fits the essentials, like gels, electrolyte packs—you name it. It also has a reflective logo to help with visibility if you're running after dark. Another plus: the split side hem gives you a full range of motion, which is great for picking up the pace.

Our only real gripe is that we wish the waistband were a bit thicker for more tummy support. It’s also low-rise, which might not be everyone’s thing—but Lauture said she was surprised by how comfortable it felt and that it stayed put during her runs.

In my experience, it's difficult to find flowy workout shorts that don't show too much skin, but this option from Alo shifts that paradigm. It's light and airy with its woven material, but it doesn't have any open seams, so you don't have to worry about the wind catching it in the wrong way (IYKYK). Plus, it has a built-in brief, which is awesome for added protection.

I also love the thick elastic waistband, which not only adds a fun design element, but hits at the perfect height on our stomach to offer a nice contouring effect. There's also an invisible side pocket to store all your small essentials while on the go.My favorite part about this short is that it's never clingy, so it doesn't ride up the thigh or need constant readjusting while you're working out. I’ve owned it for months and recently tested it during a 45-minute strength and HIIT workout as well as an hour-long cross-training workout, and I never felt over-exposed or uncomfortable in it. It's roomy, but also holds you in. Plus, the fabric dries super fast, so you're in good hands if you get super sweaty.It does run one size big, which you should note when adding to cart. However, if you like shorts that are roomier, I can confirm that this one still gets high marks even when it's a size too big. In my experience, it still felt full-coverage, airy, and lightweight.

Patagonia’s Baggies Short is a warm-weather favorite among our editors—especially the ones who love spending time outdoors, like myself. The short fared exceptionally well during hot hikes over the summer but does just as well in the offseason indoors or while active outside.

It’s easy to throw on, thanks to its comfy fit that completely avoids any unwanted cling (no camel toe here, thank you very much). Plus, it’s made from quick-drying, breathable nylon, so I never have to worry about feeling weighed down. I’m personally stoked to wear this short again while hiking in Cotopaxi National Park in Ecuador.

While it definitely has a sporty vibe, it’s versatile enough to wear around the city, too. In black, it feels laid-back and low-key—perfect for running errands without looking like you just left the gym. Toss on an oversized sweatshirt or a longline sports bra, and you’ve got an effortless, off-duty look. And if you get caught in the rain or decide to take a dip? No stress—it’s water-repellent, so it won’t stay soaked.

The 5-inch inseam is another win: not too long, not too short—just the right amount of leg without worrying about coverage. Prefer something shorter? The Baggie also comes in a 2.5-inch version, which is great if you want a more cropped fit.

Fabric is everything when it comes to workout shorts—look for lightweight, sweat-wicking materials that move with you, not against you. According to Saladino, it's best to steer clear of cotton when looking for athletic shorts, as it doesn't wick away moisture as well as materials like polyester and nylon. After all, you want to make sure you're staying totally dry in your workout shorts (because who wants sweat stains down there?).

Most shorts on this list are high-rise, which we found to have the most coverage and look the most flattering during our workouts, as they offer flattering tummy control. Many high-rise shorts also have a drawstring, which helps you customize the fit so it doesn't slip down or ride up while you're getting a sweat on. Some of the options we tried were low-rise, but we ended up ditching most of them because we didn't love the fit. However, the Arc'teryx pair on this list is low-rise, and we actually love that it sits nicely on our hips and looks flattering.

When it comes to the best length for workout shorts, you want to think about the inseam length, AKA the distance between the crotch area and the bottom of the short. There are some longer options for those who prefer more leg coverage (ideal for burpees and squats!), and super short options on this list if you like a lightweight mini short for running or walking. After testing, we prefer something right in the middle that makes us feel nimble but also provides coverage, like our favorite of the bunch, The Gym People High Waist Shorts.

After testing, we found that some shorts are better for specific activities. For example, the Beyond Yoga pair is great for yoga because it’s super stretchy and buttery soft, so it’s easy to move in, whether you’re in downward dog or trying to master crow pose. On the other hand, the Arc'teryx pair is low-rise, super light, and has a snug fit, making it ideal for running since it feels weightless and doesn't slow us down.

We first compiled this list in July 2024. Since then, Women’s Health editors have continued to put biker shorts, compression shorts, running shorts, and more through their paces to find the best options for every workout. For this November 2026 update, I re-tested some of our faves and put more than 20 shorts through their paces, evaluating them based on fit, rise, coverage, breathability, weight, and more. The testing process was led by me, with help from style contributor Lily Wohlner and stylists Rose Lauture and Kristen Saladino. Our evaluation involved multiple phases, consulting workout fanatics on the Women's Health team, and most importantly, testing the shorts firsthand. We subjected each short to everything from running to fast walks, HIIT workouts to Pilates and even cycling. The narrowed-down list below includes the six shorts that impressed us most.

#4936. 15 Best Doormats That Are Durable and Design-Forward (2026)

Displaying a welcoming doormats at your home’s threshold is a crucial opportunity to make a strong first impression on visitors. But it’s not just about wooing your guests upon arrival—they should also have some staying power against the elements and an onslaught of muddy boots this winter.

Thankfully, we found plenty of heavy-duty, high-quality doormats that are both handsome and durable. Many of these options feature natural fibers made from coir, which is mildew-resistant, absorbent, and can survive any kind of weather conditions and foot traffic it endures. Eco-friendly jute is another natural material common among doormat designs—favored for its organic look and its ability to trap dirt while still looking clean. Our top picks include doormats we’ve tested in our own homes as well as a few exciting options from brands we trust, so we don’t suggest (figuratively) dragging your feet on these great designs.

Ruggable’s entire door mat catalog is machine washable, which feels like a non-negotiable for an item literally made to trap dirt. Senior commerce editor Nashia Baker found a kindred match in this pick, telling us that “the balance of whimsical lines and shapes makes walking through the door a harmonious experience.” She also noted that it’s “incredibly durable,” and after months of high-traffic it “can handle any wet or muddy shoes that land on it without getting waterlogged.” Non-slip backing keeps it (and you) from sliding around.

Lean into a modern nautical vibe (think: this contemporary Long Island escape) with Serena & Lily’s chunky mat that looks like it was woven from stolen sailboat rope. The natural/coastal blue colorway offers just a hint of color, while monochromatic options that weave in multiple shades of blue and white make a more vibrant statement.

Sometimes all you need to make a statement is a simple pattern. This honeycomb design is subtle, mildew-resistant, shed-free, and fade-safe. A rubber backing means there won’t be any slipping and it’s designed to hold water—the raised border design helps contain up to 1.5 gallons of water per square yard.

Quilt-like lines feed into a larger geometric pattern in this doormat design that still feels simple but very modern. The grid of black rectangular lines reads as a neutral, and the elongated shape covers more area than some of its peers on this list, so we’d recommend it for an entry hallway or wider doorsteps.

This Heymat doormat is a durable option for covered porches and entryways. Not suitable for true outdoor use (on an uncovered patio or anywhere susceptible to the elements), this Heymat doormat is highly absorbent and soft underfoot. Shopping market editor Kate McGregor’s family owns a few mats from this brand, which they use as an oversized entryway mat in the mudroom for muddy boots and dog paws, as well as a bathmat in the guest bathroom. “This multi-colored mat has held up so well against summer mud and dropped birdseed, despite its pastel grid design,” she says. “Even after five years, the colors have stayed vibrant, and the mat never gets soggy.” Plus, whether sprayed down or shaken, she notes that the cleanup is very easy. “I might protest if my mom ever decides to replace it.”

A departure from the traditional rectangular doormat shape, this Toast alternative offers colorful texture in one compact oval shape that’s fully reversible. This one is crafted from woven and braided jute strands that are ideal for trapping loose dirt and debris. For those looking for an alternative to standard brown jute styles, these alternating patterns are pretty mesmerizing.

If you’ve got more floor space to fill in your greeting room, smaller sizes of The Citizenry’s jute rugs could be exactly what you’ve been looking for. At 24” x 36,” this hand braided mat has a refined look thanks to the contrasting border design, and it’ll be a nice surface to station wet or damp shoes so you’re not damaging the floor.

In our doormat quest, we also found this woven gem from Matilda Goad’s MG&Co. with looped fringing that looks like scalloped edges. The deep burgundy tone will help hide visible mud stains (though the jute weave can also be easily hosed down when it’s time for a clean). It’s also available in a longer, thinner silhouette to help cover sprawling patios.

Floral without feeling overly whimsical (no shame if that’s your vibe, though), Anthropologie’s sweet, embossed doormat is a simple option for anyone with an already-decorated entryway. With an abundance of five-star ratings, lots of reviews praise the design's versatile look and durable material makeup.

The raised, slatted design of Crate & Barrel’s unfinished teakwood doormat keeps moisture, grime, and dirt away sans-bristles. It’s also great for indoor use, perhaps as a minimalist bath mat. Be mindful that teak patinas over time due to weather and regular wear and tear, shifting from a golden wood to a grayish color.

The bold tulip motif on this doormat has a cheerful Scandi-folk style that can brighten your front entry even in the dead of winter. When it starts to look a little worse for wear, the mat easily lifts off its non-slip base for machine washing. In a spot that receives near-constant foot traffic, the ability to refresh it from season to season will be a godsend.

Danish brand HAY is known for their lively color combinations, and their doormats are no exception. With interlocking strands of navy and pink rope, bookended by charming red trim, this pick welcomes guests in with a jolt of maximalist energy. The vegetable fiber strands offer a strong and durable natural alternative to plastic: Shake it out and spray it down with water to clean it and keep the colors fresh.

A stylish coir braid gives this under-$30 doormat a higher-end look. The thick weave creates an almost padded texture, designed to expertly track dirt as your shoe treads catch on the material. With its lattice-like appearance, we envision this doormat at the front door of your Cotswolds-inspired farmhouse, or perhaps a coastal home that could use another natural texture to contrast the white and blue color palette.

Leave it to Sarah Sherman Samuel to create a great doormat. The AD100 designer, arguably most known for Mandy Moore’s Altadena home, offers a twist on the traditional rectangle. Uneven stripes with cutouts give your entryway a modern edge. The coir is dependable, and the black accents help to disguise the inevitable mess.

CB2’s doormat selection is predominantly composed of versatile Chilewich designs—like this monochromatic pattern that feels like a fashionable take on television static. Designed with functionality first, the shag mat uses antimicrobial yarn to keep itself tidy. It also has a no-slip backing to keep it fixed near your doorstep, even when your shoes need a serious wipe down.

What should you look for in the best outdoor doormats?

Although design is important, you also want to make sure that your doormat is low profile enough to fit under your door and also has a non-slip backing to keep your guests from busting it before they make it into your home. (Talk about a first impression!) Materials like PVC with rubber backing are key for the latter, while 100% coir doormats give your entryway a more natural look and are more ideal for trapping dirt and debris.

The answer is a tentative yes. You’re always going to want to see what the manufacturer recommends and it, of course, depends on where you live. Doormats are always made for outdoor use, but various climates will wear down the materials differently. Frequent rain and snow might soften jute while constant sunshine will fade most textiles. An easy solution, if you aren’t sure what your mat can withstand, is to drag your doormat into the mudroom or somewhere with a bit of shelter whenever there’s big weather on its way.

#4934. Unocoin keeps deposits and withdrawals halted over suspect transfers

Unocoin said the transfers were signed and broadcast outside BitGo’s platform, and BitGo said the account freeze worked as intended.

Update (Nov. 13, 2026, 12:30 pm UTC): This article has been updated to include BitGo’s response and clarify that the account freeze applied to activity routed through BitGo’s platform.

Indian cryptocurrency exchange Unocoin has kept deposits and withdrawals suspended as it investigates suspicious wallet transfers and a breach of its own systems.

BitGo froze Unocoin’s enterprise account on Nov. 6 at the exchange’s request. Unocoin said the freeze appeared to have worked as intended and that the transfers were signed and broadcast onchain outside BitGo’s platform, according to its Friday update.

“Our review found that the transaction examined was signed using the user and backup keys held by Unocoin and broadcast externally onchain, without BitGo’s participation. BitGo’s systems were not breached in connection with that transaction,” BitGo said in a statement to Cointelegraph.

The company said the freeze applied only to activity routed through its platform and that the transfers were signed using keys Unocoin held outside BitGo’s systems.

Unocoin said it was investigating possible use of the wallet’s backup signing option and whether any cryptocurrency was lost. The exchange did not respond to Cointelegraph’s request for more information before publication.

Unocoin first detected unauthorized activity on Nov. 6 and suspended all services on Monday after detecting further activity. On Thursday, it disclosed outgoing transfers from an Ethereum address associated with its BitGo wallets and said its infrastructure had been compromised.

A Nov. 5 warning from India’s cybersecurity agency described an AI-assisted campaign targeting crypto exchanges and other financial firms. No connection to Unocoin’s incident has been established.

#4932. Israeli police arrest five in $5M WhatsApp crypto trading probe

Police suspect the group drew up fictitious loan agreements to disguise crypto trading proceeds it transferred directly into bank accounts.

Israeli police arrested five people on Tuesday in a money laundering investigation involving about 16 million shekels ($5 million) in crypto transactions arranged through a WhatsApp group.

Investigators from the National Unit for Combating Economic Crime within Lahav 433 suspect the group provided crypto services without a license and failed to report transactions to Israel’s tax authorities. Police allege the group used fictitious agreements to make crypto proceeds transferred into bank accounts look like loans, according to The Jerusalem Post.

Authorities seized wallets, computers and tens of thousands of shekels in cash while searching the suspects’ homes. Investigators questioned the five on suspicion of money laundering, fraud and providing financial asset services without a license.

Israel’s Tax Authority announced two other arrests on Oct. 6 in cases involving suspected failures to report crypto activity. One involved trades worth tens of millions of dollars. In the other, an Ashdod resident allegedly failed to report income from about $13 million in crypto trades between 2019 and 2021.

A November 2024 audit by Israel’s State Comptroller found that about 500 people reported crypto activity each year on average from 2018 to 2022, out of at least 200,000 potential filers.

#4931. The 6 Best On Shoes for Walking of 2026, Tested By Fitness Editors and Podiatrists

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

As a Women’s Health style writer, I regularly test the latest releases from all the major sneaker brands. On kicks are some of my favorites, and our editors and A-list celebs love ‘em too (including Zendaya). The Swiss brand has seen impressive growth over the past year, becoming a major competitor among sneaker giants like Nike and Adidas. On’s signature CloudTec cushioning not only makes you feel like you’re “walking on clouds,” but it’s also right on trend and a major style statement for wellness girlies.

We've named these kicks some of the best running shoes for plantar fasciitis, but after vigorous testing, we absolutely love On shoes for walking, too. Podiatrist Brad Schaeffer, DPM, says he walks around the city daily in his On sneakers because they make him feel supported and comfortable and accommodate his Dr. Scholl's insoles. "Thanks to the thicker sole and rounded heel, they provide that perfect mix of function, stability, and cushion without sacrificing any category," he says.

On has a large roster of comfortable sneakers, so it can be tricky to know where to start to find the perfect pair. That's why we tapped Schaeffer, podiatrist Daniel Geller, DPM, and Women's Health fitness editors to give us the lowdown on what to look for when shopping for the best On Cloud shoes for walking: in this case, weight, cushion, stability, and heel-to-toe drop.

Keep reading to see our favorites, and be sure to check out our 4-Week Walking Plan for the perfect workout to break in your new kicks.

After testing several pairs of On shoes, the Cloudrunner 3—a cushier, more supportive upgrade from the Cloudrunner 2—takes the top spot for a few key reasons. Executive health and fitness director Jacqueline Andriakos has tested more than a dozen On shoes and says the Cloudrunner 3 has become a go-to in her sneaker collection lately. That’s because the shoe has a relatively lightweight feel with tons of stability.

That balance comes from the sole, which is made with On’s Helion Superfoam. This material, made from thermoplastic polyurethane, blends firm and flexible foam components to create a lightweight, responsive, and well-cushioned feel. The mix of stiffer and softer sections absorbs impact from every step and actually helps propel you forward. The Cloudrunner 3 is actually a touch heavier than its predecessor (by only 0.7 ounces), but we chalk it up to the upgraded plush heel collar and wider base that offer a bit more comfort and stability. I’ve noticed this shoe is super durable, holding up to months of wear and tear on city sidewalks. During my walks in this shoe, I appreciate that I don’t feel overly bouncy, but the cushioning is still noticeable and light enough to help me feel grounded.“At nine months pregnant, I need to prioritize stability and comfort over everything else in a sneaker right now, and the On Cloudrunner 3s delivered for me,” Andriakos says. “It feels firm and supportive (and not overly cushioned), which has noticeably reduced my pelvic and low back pain when I’m on my feet all day and walking a lot.” She’s also been wearing it for hybrid strength-and-cardio workouts, and while it’s not a super-flat traditional lifting shoe, the fairly neutral sole and structured shape and feel make it surprisingly versatile. “Plus, the toe box is on the wider side and roomy enough for my swollen feet, so my toes can actually breathe,” Andriakos adds.

After about four months of testing an alarming amount of shoes, the On Cloudtilt Remix is my everyday go-to. That’s because this sneaker takes everything we love about the original Cloudtilt and gives it a fashion-forward upgrade with a techy upper designed with “X-ray layers,” or semi-transparent mesh overlays that look super sleek.

This shoe is basically built for walking, too, thanks to the CloudTec Phase midsole, a walking-focused cushioning system designed so each “cloud” compresses in sequence, delivering a smooth, plush ride. The result is an exceptionally smooth heel-to-toe transition that feels natural and effortless during long days on your feet. It also has a moderate 7 mm heel-to-toe drop, meaning it distributes weight evenly throughout the lower body and helps keep the foot in a neutral walking position, making it a pretty universal pick.

Underfoot, the cushioning lands squarely in the Goldilocks zone. The Helion superfoam provides plenty of impact absorption, but the ride never feels overly soft or marshmallow-like. Instead, it delivers a lightly responsive, cushioned feel that keeps your feet comfortable during long walks, travel days, and hours of sightseeing without sacrificing ground feel or stability. Lightweight, stylish, and genuinely built for all-day movement, the Cloudtilt Remix is the On sneaker I reach for when I want my shoes to work as hard as the rest of my outfit. The sleek, streamlined look is super easy to style with everything from tennis skirts to joggers to track pants. If you ask me, it’s kinda the perfect shoe that combines everything on this list into one sleek kick.

My one note is that I worry about the layered mesh upper being difficult to clean if the shoe gets too dirty. Luckily, I’ve managed to keep it pretty clean, but I avoid wearing this shoe in wet weather or otherwise messy conditions.

Hate tying your shoes? The Cloudnova Form 2 might be your new favorite—thanks to its easy slip-on, slip-off design, which Andriakos swears by. That said, it still has laces if you want to tighten things up for a more secure fit. This is my everyday shoe when I’m heading out the door to run errands or pop out for a walk but don’t feel like wearing anything bulky or something that needs a full lace adjustment (just lazy girl things!). It looks super cute with sweatpants and leggings, and a boxy t-shirt on top.

Comfort-wise, the Cloudnova Form is a win right out of the box. During my testing, I found that there was no break-in period needed (big ups). The moderately-cushioned sole is super balanced, which makes it ideal for long walks and power strolls, and Andriakos especially likes that it doesn’t have the super-prominent “bubble” look that many On shoes are known for. Instead, it has a lower-cut silhouette that feels a bit more grounded and less bouncy.

Another plus: The Form 2 is made with a breathable mesh upper and a soft microfiber tongue, so your feet stay cool and comfortable even on warm or extra-active days. On the downside, it runs small, so it’s a good idea to size it up by half. Also worth noting: it has a high heel-to-toe drop (14 mm), which can put extra stress on the knees and hips. If you deal with pain in those areas, you might want to skip this one.

On only offers wide sizing for certain models, but this shoe has a spacious toe box for a roomy fit. Fitness contributor Nicolette Accardi has bunions and never experiences pain when wearing it. “Most sneakers that don’t come in wide sizing tend to irritate and rub against my bunions, which makes them throb, but not the Cloudmonster,” she says. “The toe box is surprisingly a perfect fit and lets me walk around for hours pain-free.”

This new version of the shoe delivers a cradling sensation while the foam slightly compresses to conform to your feet. The sensation is pillow-like under the foot while also offering a stable feel. Fitness contributor Talene Appleton notes that it's her all-time fave On walking shoe for its high-stack cushion, meaning it has a very thick foam between your foot and the ground. The 3 gets back to the Cloudmonster’s roots and becomes a good running shoe for intermediate to advanced runners again. That’s thanks to a speedboard that promotes a forward rolling motion, along with the aforementioned maxed cushioning. This has added only a little weight from the last model (6.6 ounces to 8.5), so you don’t have to worry about this shoe holding you back during long walks or runs.

"Whenever I want to feel super comfortable in my shoes but don't want that tight, locked-in feeling like I do when I'm running, the Cloudmonster is my go-to," Appleton says. She wore the shoe while moving into her fourth-floor Brooklyn walk-up, and notes it kept her feet comfortable all day. And while it’s great for getting your steps in, this shoe has that chunky look that’s super on trend right now. I love pairing it with tailored pants and a boxy t-shirt on top for that upgraded activewear vibe.

The heel-to-toe drop is also on the smaller side at six millimeters, which Accardi says distributes impact evenly on the knees, hips, and ankles. “As someone with knee issues, taking the load off my knees is essential, especially post-run,” she says. If you’re a heel striker and don’t struggle with pain in these areas, the Cloudrunner 2 could be a better fit.

If your workouts don’t fit neatly into one category, the On Cloud X 4 is the sneaker you’ll want on standby. Designed specifically for mixed training, it’s comfortable, responsive, and stable, making it equally suited for walking, HIIT training, and gym sessions. Unlike some of On’s chunkier models, the Cloud X 4 has a slightly lower-profile silhouette that looks and feels sleeker on foot, pairing easily with everyday outfits and activewear.

The shoe features On’s signature CloudTec cushioning, which delivers a comfortable, impact-absorbing ride without feeling overly squishy. Andriakos, who logs a high daily step count, says it’s become one of her favorite shoes for long walks because the cushioning feels nice and plush while maintaining a grounded feel. “The mesh upper is super breathable, so my feet don’t feel overheated and sweaty after long walks, and small design details (like the cool X lace pattern from above!) make it feel really polished,” she says.

The supportive lacing system creates a secure, locked-in feel that feels stable during lateral movements and dynamic workouts. “I’ve worn it to HIIT classes, and it feels super supportive, though I’d still opt for a flatter, more structured shoe for traditional lifting,” Andriakos says. The mesh upper is a nice touch, too, keeping things super breathable so your feet don’t get overheated or sweaty on long walks.

The On Cloud 6 Coast is a refreshed take on the brand’s classic On Cloud—but this ultra-lightweight version takes it even further. It keeps all the upgrades of the latest model, including the original slip-on, no-lace design and On’s signature CloudTec cushioning system. The big win here? It weighs in at just 6.5 ounces. That means your ultra-cushioned shoe is now perfect for traveling, long days on your feet, or hot, humid commutes. It’s built with an updated mesh that’s super breathable and ventilated—you can even wear this shoe barefoot!It also features a wider opening for a more inclusive, easy-on fit. I really appreciated this feature as a wide-footed girly. It also has a moderate heel-to-toe drop of 8 mm, making it a great universal walking shoe. Bottom line: this shoe is made to handle just about anything, which makes it a must-have in your rotation.

This shoe has a medium cushion level for that sweet spot that’s comfortable and light on your feet without being overly plush. The CloudTec midsole does a great job absorbing impact, making it a solid choice for everything from sightseeing and airport sprints to casual daily walks. The lightweight build almost disappears on your foot, which is exactly what you want when you’re packing light or spending hours exploring.

The tradeoff for all that packability and featherlight comfort is support. The flexible upper and minimalist construction can feel a bit flimsy compared to more structured walking shoes, especially if you need extra arch support or stability.

On sneakers are extremely comfortable, but Schaeffer says that's because most of its shoes have a bit of weight to them. If a shoe is too lightweight (under four ounces), it sacrifices function and stability, he says. But, don't get it twisted—these don't feel like bricks on your feet either. Most On shoes are between four and 10 ounces, which means they're the perfect medium weight that doesn’t slack on support.

A heel-to-toe drop, sometimes called a midsole drop, is the difference in height between the heel and forefoot (toe area). Schaeffer says to look for a walking shoe with a heel-to-toe drop that puts your foot in a neutral position, which will be different for everyone’s unique foot and step pattern.

Support and stability are the number one qualities you should look for in a walking shoe, says Geller. He notes that when arches are supported, you create an "excellent" platform to launch from, meaning the feet are in the ideal position for takeoff and landing. This can help avoid foot injuries down the line.

Geller also says that many good walking shoes, including motion control shoes, will have medial posting—a firm wedge in the arch that holds up the heel—and firm cushioning for more support. "Firmer cushioning will resist the inward roll of the foot [overpronation], controlling the knees and hips better," he says.

If stability is a priority for you, also consider shoes with a broader sole to minimize excess movement. The increased material along the sides and front of your foot creates a wider platform, which is naturally resistant to feet rolling or wobbling, says Geller. In other words, it's a great feature for walkers who overpronate.

"Whenever you’re looking for a good walking shoe, you want to find a great mix of comfort and stability," says Schaeffer. You want a shoe that’s comfortable on your feet, but the level of cushioning will vary depending on your specific foot needs.

Wearing running shoes for walking isn’t inherently bad, but it’s not always the best idea either. Shoes designed specifically for running tend to have significantly more cushioning to absorb the higher impact that comes with each stride. “This isn't necessary for walking and reduces your feel of the ground, which is problematic for those with any balance issues or previous falls," Milica McDowell, a doctor of physical therapy, previously told Women’s Health.

Running shoes often have a very tight fit for higher performance, a narrow toe box, or are highly supported in the arch, which are features a lifestyle walker does not need, says McDowell. That’s why, in most cases, walkers are recommended to opt for a shoe designed specifically for walking (or one labeled for walking and running).

To curate a list of the best On walking shoes, I tested On kicks for two years, alongside fitness contributor Talene Appleton, NASM-CPT, fitness contributor Nicolette Accardi, NASM-CPT, style contributor Lily Wohlner, and executive health and fitness director Jacqueline Andriakos.

We wore them during long and short walks for at least several hours at a time. We evaluated each shoe based on:

I also sought advice from two podiatrists on what to look for when shopping for the best shoes for walking, as well as their professional thoughts on our favorite On picks.We originally had three picks in this guide when we first wrote this article in May 2024, but added three more favorites to this list after two years–plus of additional testing. We found that the new and older winners all provide top-notch comfort, cushioning, support, and stability through all our long walks.

#4930. 8 Best Hotel Mattress Picks for a Five-Star Staycation (2026)

The hotel mattress probably isn't on your vacation itinerary, but it can make or break the trip. A lumpy, unsupportive bed can derail even the most carefully planned getaway. A really good one, though, might become an unexpected highlight—the kind that has you looking forward to bedtime and quietly checking the mattress label before checkout.

Recreating that experience at home doesn't require another plane ticket. Some of our favorite properties, including design-forward waterfront retreats and charming bed-and-breakfasts, put just as much thought into their mattresses as they do their interiors. Many turn to brands like Saatva, Ostermoor, and Casper to outfit their guest rooms; others, like the W Hotels, have signature mattresses you can purchase directly. We've rounded up our favorites, such as options with plush pillow tops, supportive coils, and pressure-relieving foam, to help you bring home the best part of your stay. The room service, unfortunately, is still up to you.

For consistency, all the prices reflect queen-size mattresses.

A stay at the Ritz-Carlton is typically reflected by its refined, elegant bedrooms. The property’s eponymous bed invites the same feeling. At 14 inches, it’s a higher-profile mattress that can help make the bed the centerpiece of the room. One of the standout qualities is its coil system, as it includes 900-plus individual springs for great edge support to help keep the sides from sagging as well as promote motion isolation—a necessary factor for couples who don’t want to sense each other’s every move.

Serta is one of the most well-known mattress manufacturers for high-end hotels, such as the Waldorf-Astoria. While many luxury properties feature custom beds from the namesake brand, it doesn’t mean you can’t shop at popular retailers such as Amazon. You’d never guess it, but this premium bed is priced under $500 (making it the most affordable on our list). While Serta offers memory foam and hybrid versions of its beds, this pillow-top innerspring mattress has been a favorite in our shopping writer Julia Harrison’s space, and she says it lives up to its “Five-Star” name.

It’s filled with three zones of coil support that keep her free of back and neck problems, and the quilted cover gives her something soft to dream about each night. “I’m really not one for pomp and frills in my mattress—I’m a firm believer that a good mattress has very little going on besides a somewhat plush top to keep you from feeling any sort of spring mechanism going on inside,” she says in her mattress review. “I instantly slept well on this mattress I think because it’s quite simply: a great mattress.” Bonus: It’s a mattress-in-a-box, so it can fit easily through narrow doors and hallways once it’s delivered, and inflate to its full size in less than a day’s time after unboxing, according to Harrison. Just in case you’re on the fence, it comes with a 100-day sleep trial so you can really see if it’s right for you before committing.

The Six Bells Countryside Inn opened its doors in the bucolic Hudson Valley in 2025, and it’s already earned two Michelin Keys. In each of the 11 carefully and whimsically designed bedrooms at this retreat, you’ll find handcrafted mattresses and bedding from New York-born brand Ostermoor. Dating back to 1853, Ostermoor’s mattresses have a storied history. The beds have innovated to foam and pocketed coil inner layers and designer covers in recent years, and we can prove they’re worth the splurge.

“From the moment I plopped down on the mattress, I was amazed by how comfortable and supportive it was,” shares contributor Zoë Sessums. “It strikes a perfect balance between spring and cushion—just the right amount of give without ever feeling too soft. I consistently wake up feeling rested and supported.” Firm without feeling rigid, this mattress looks as good as it feels, too. “The tufted top, the blue and white ticking pattern, the hand-stitched details—it feels like a piece of luxury furniture, not just a place to sleep,” Sessums adds, later writing, “I would recommend this to someone who values design and craftsmanship as much as comfort.”

Saatva has found its way into charming bed-and-breakfasts and boutique retreats across the country, including Pasadena's historic Bissell House (an 1887 Victorian filled with antique furnishings) and the Cornell Inn in the Berkshires (known for its colorful, individually designed guest rooms). You can bring that same inviting comfort home with the Saatva Classic, which comes with a plush three-inch Euro pillow top, a responsive dual-coil system, and targeted lumbar support. “It’s firm (which I prefer), regulates temperature well, and is extremely durable,” our tester Erin Kaplan, vice president of communications at Conde Nast, says. “I alternate between sleeping on my side and sleeping on my stomach, and this mattress is great for both positions.”

Choose from three firmness levels—plush soft, luxury firm, or firm—, eight different sizes, and two mattress heights to find your ideal fit. Feeling extra? Saatva also offers two adjustable bases that elevate your head and feet at the touch of a button, including a premium Plus model for an even more indulgent breakfast in bed. A 365-night trial gives you plenty of time to sleep on your decision before committing.

At 1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge, even the beds have a view. Sweeping views of the Manhattan skyline set the scene, with reclaimed wood floors, rich leather headboards, and locally crafted details like crate-inspired closets and Fresnel glass light fixtures bringing warmth and character to the rooms. With custom Keetsa mattresses in every room, you might find yourself hitting snooze despite the spectacular view.

Back at home, the Keetsa Pillow Plus offers its own take on hotel-worthy comfort. It's something of a Goldilocks mattress: not too soft, not too firm, but just right. A three-inch pillow top combines body-contouring memory foam with responsive comfort foam to help cushion pressure points, and a soft, moisture-wicking cover designed to keep overheating at bay. Individually wrapped coils provide cushioning and support while minimizing motion transfer, so even if your bedmate tosses and turns, you can stay blissfully unaware.

When husband-and-wife duo Ely and Danielle Franko transformed a dated Catskills ski hostel into The Henson, a 16-room boutique hotel, they had a pretty good idea of what makes a great night's sleep. The couple painstakingly restored the property themselves, filling its rooms with vintage furniture, locally sourced finds, and hand-applied wallpaper. But when it came to mattresses, they didn't have to look far for inspiration: They chose the same Casper Dream Hybrid they sleep on at home. In fact, they loved it so much that they insisted on king-size mattresses in every room, even the smallest ones. The hybrid design combines responsive springs with breathable foam and three zones of support that help keep your spine aligned. Its medium feel is meant to offer a little give without leaving you sinking into the mattress, making it a crowd-pleasing choice for your own guest room. After all, the best hosts know a good night's sleep is part of the hospitality.

Hot sleepers, here’s a mattress for you. The Four Season’s signature mattress features a couple of core cooling bed qualities: proprietary cooling gel foam layers with channeled designs that promote airflow throughout the mattress, as well as a patented DualCool top layer that draws heat and moisture away from the body and keeps the bed fresh with its antimicrobial properties. The cooling mattress is designed for sleepers who need extra structure on their bed. This posh number has targeted support for the lower back area and zeroes in on alignment regardless of your sleep style.

The W Hotels are widely popular because of the bold design across the properties worldwide. To mirror this aesthetic, you can cover the brand’s mattress with colorful bedding to let your personal style shine. When it comes to the bed itself, it is defined by a plush top quilted damask design to ease side sleepers into a peaceful slumber. It’s made for people who need extra support too, though, including an individually-wrapped coil system, five-zone support system, and comfort layers for added cushioning and pressure relief.

Which Kind of Mattress Do Five-Star Hotels Use?

Most luxury hotels use hybrid mattresses in their suites to strike the right balance of softness and support, thanks to pocketed coils and layers of foam. These are also typically medium-firm mattresses since a plush mattress can be uncomfortable for some sleep positions like stomach sleepers. Ultra-firm beds are often too stiff for side sleeping and may not align with guests' expectations who are looking for soft mattresses to sink into on their vacations.

If you want to refresh your mattress without the hefty price tag of buying a new one, a mattress topper or featherbed could be a solid transitional pick. The Ritz-Carlton and W Hotels promote one made with white duck feathers, Mandarin Oriental’s exclusive topper comprises white goose feathers, Waldorf Astoria beds feature a down-alternative fill, and Marriott’s selection is polyester.

There’s no one-size-fits-all here, so it really comes down to your preferred loftiness and weight. Duck and goose feathers are heavier than others fills, though duck is slightly less fluffy and won’t trap heat as well. Down-alternatives, like polyester, are more allergen-friendly and “a good option for those who prefer to be vegan in their home,” Danielle Trotter, the former textiles technical designer at West Elm, previously shared.

What Is the Thickness of a Hotel Mattress?

Hotel mattresses usually average 12 inches in thickness. This makes it easier to hop in and out of bed, especially when using a box spring that can add extra height. Plus, it prevents the need for deep pocket sheets.

How Can I Recreate the Hotel Bed Experience at Home?

We’ve explored the entire topic on how to make your bedroom feel like a hotel, and aside from finding a new bed with a medium-firm feel, we’ve learned that percale sheets and down pillows are pretty much a must to complete the setup. When it comes to the former, hotel sheets are usually made with organic cotton percale because the fabric looks and feels crisp, giving that refined aesthetic a boutique stay is known for. Usually a 200 thread count is a good rule of thumb to look out for since this means there’s plenty of airflow between the threads for a breathable feel. Hotel pillows are usually filled with down feathers since they’re so lofty and soft, but a down alternative is just as good in case you’re an allergy-prone sleeper (just look for materials like hypoallergenic gel fibers since they’re known for being squishy without falling flat, just like a feather-filled pillow).

What Is the Difference Between Memory Foam and Latex?

Traditional memory foam has a body-contouring effect that allows your body to sink into your mattress, reducing motion transfer (a must for bedmates!). Meanwhile, latex foam offers more responsiveness (or bounce) and overall support. As Neslihan Ozdemir, founder of Girl on the Mattress, previously told AD, latex also holds up well over time and is temperature-regulating. Latex foam mattresses (and some memory foam options) are certified organic, making them eco-friendly foam picks, too.

Known as the most common mattress type, innerspring mattresses feature a bed of coils. There’s quite a range to these mattresses: Basic versions have a grid of steel coils, while premier options have a pillow top and pocketed coil technology, meaning each coil is individually wrapped to help with motion isolation. Ozdemir added that innerspring is best for people who sleep on the edge of the bed or are heavier in weight. If you prefer a more plush mattress, but still want the support of those coils, consider a hybrid mattress, which is layered with soft foam.
