#4862. The 9 Best Sunscreens of 2026, Tested by Dermatologists and Editors

Just in time for the last-minute holiday trips.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

I’ve written extensively about sunscreen since 2019, most recently in our guide to SPF facts, spray sunscreen, and how one dermatologist uses it as a dry shampoo hack. But if you’re looking for a one-and-done power list of the best sunscreens of 2026, this is it.

And sunscreen’s benefits don’t stop there. Sun damage accumulates from daily activities like driving and sitting in front of a window, says dermatologist Hadley King, MD. That means even during the fall and winter, we should still double down on sunscreen. Here’s how to buy SPF like a dermatologist and beauty editor.

As a picky beauty editor, it really takes a lot for a product to truly impress me. Isdin Eryfotona Ageless Sunscreen has become a staple in my routine, and I will gladly continue repurchasing bottles to ensure my skin is protected for life. So what makes it stand out the most? The impressive ingredient list. Allow Dr. Goldenberg to explain. "Isdin's SPF contains ‘repairsomes,’ which help with reversing sun damage in skin cells," he says. That makes this a great pick for anyone with hyperpigmentation or sun spots, especially since the formula has a glowy, tinted finish.

I had a light sunburn last summer, and my dermatologist suggested I use this SPF. After I slathered on moisturizer and layered on this liquid sunscreen during the day, I noticed my skin was less red after just two days. I was floored because I hadn’t used any new products other than the Isdin Eryfotona Ageless. A year later, and I can confirm it’s still well worth using. My skin never breaks out, the lightweight formula absorbs quickly, and it’s water-resistant for active lifestyles. It’s also available in tinted and untinted options.

It absorbs in just a few minutes and mattifies my oily T-zone and leaves behind a soft, luminous finish. Not to mention, it doesn’t cause breakouts or irritate my skin when I’m dealing with seasonal changes and sensitivities.

If I had to be nitpicky, then the only thing I dislike about Isdin is the price. However, there’s a smaller 1.7 fl. oz bottle to help ease the pain. I’ll continue to repurchase this sunscreen because it works fabulously with my oily, acne-prone skin. It’s also helpful for my 50-something mom’s mature skin. I also converted our visual editor, Jason Speakman, into a fan—he noticed a decrease in facial redness over six months of daily use.

Neutrogena's sunscreen stick is a great product for those on the run, says Dr. Goldenberg. It's easy to apply or reapply, and it offers SPF 50 with water resistance, so people with active lifestyles really love it—just check the 10,208 perfect 5-star ratings on Amazon.

Neutrogena is cheap, travel-friendly, glides on clear, and is effective. However, we found it was too greasy for oily skin. However, if you have normal or dry skin, or just want to glow, this is the face sunscreen for you. With festival season underway, your skin will definitely “shine bright like a diamond” with the help of this sunscreen. And honestly, at just under $10, it’s worth trying.

Dr. Campbell is a fan of EltaMD's sunscreen, as are Lindsay Geller, Women's Health's lifestyle director, and Amanda Lucci, our special projects director. It contains hyaluronic acid, so Dr. Campbell often recommends it to patients with drier skin. EltaMD boasts a fragrance-free, paraben-free, and noncomedogenic formulation, making it ideal for sensitive and acne-prone skin.

The lotion has a creamy, slightly whipped texture that requires a little extra effort to blend into the skin, but it’s worth it, says Geller. However, our editors with medium to dark skin tones say this leaves a white cast on their skin, but using the Tinted version can help.

La Roche-Posay is one of the most reliable skincare brands in the game. The line is a favorite of many dermatologists I consulted, and Dr. Ranella Hirsch, MD, highlights this particular sunscreen as her top pick. She highlights the creamy formulation, which hydrates her skin and leaves it feeling velvety soft.

This is also Ritchey's new go-to. “As long as you don't smother yourself in it, I feel like it's pretty light for a sunscreen,” she says. “It's a little tacky after going on, but honestly, it was kind of nice—it definitely helped my makeup stick!” It also has a faint sunscreen smell, which she doesn't mind, since it reminds her that Anthelios Melt-In is working. She’s a self-described heavy sweater, and didn’t experience any streaking with this sunscreen.

Just keep in mind that a little goes a long way—a lesson Ritchey learned the hard way. “The first time I put too much in my hand, I looked like Larry the Lifeguard from SpongeBob SquarePants.”

Dermatologists advise applying two finger-lengths of sunscreen—about a quarter-sized amount—to your face and neck.

Read more: How Much Sunscreen You Should Use On Your Face?

Tower 28 is one of the best sunscreens that I’ve ever used. It combines all of the benefits of a broad-spectrum mineral sunscreen with foundation-like coverage in 17 shades.

It offers light-to-medium coverage that evens out my complexion without looking cakey or feeling goopy on my face. Problem spots like hyperpigmentation could use some extra love with concealer—Tower 28 makes a sweet one—but I don’t feel insecure if those spots show through with this sunscreen. It took me some trial and error to discover my exact shade, but I landed on the color 40 Silver Lake on my face and use 55 Temescal as a bronzer for a deep golden warmth.

Application is also a breeze—it applies nicely with the warmth of my fingers, but I get the most coverage when using a densely packed brush like my BK Beauty 101 Foundation Brush. I just apply the SPF to my face, buff the fluffy bristles in small, circular motions across my face, and I experience zero streaks.

Knowing that richer sunscreen shades can be a real let-down, I hit up digital designer Taryn Colbert to give this one a whirl. She uses the color 55 and puts its color payoff and longevity to the test. Tower 28 applies evenly to her bare skin and feels like nothing is on her face. Since she doesn’t have any texture or acne issues, she didn’t notice any splotches or separation with extra oil. I also have oily skin and noticed some pore emphasis on my cheeks after a few hours of wear, but honestly, touching up with oil-blotting sheets and a thin, fresh layer of SPF helps.

While Colbert and I agree with Tower 28’s sentiment that the colors are flexible, it would still be nice to have a wider range of undertones in the tan and deep shades. Still, it’s the SPF that replaces my foundation each summer and one I recommend to anyone who doesn’t want to compromise on sun protection or cosmetic coverage.

Powder sunscreen is the most underrated formulation—and Brush on Block is my favorite. It comes in a tube that features soft bristles that I dust over my face like a setting powder. It’s mess-free, making it ideal for touch-ups on the go. The broad-spectrum sunscreen is also water-resistant, so I can dust it on while poolside without worry.

But above all, it earned major snaps from Dr. King, who uses it on her face and scalp as a dry shampoo hack. Beyond perking up your hair by absorbing oil, it can add volume and texture by coating your strands with fine powders, making your hair appear fuller without sticky residue, says Dr. Goldenberg. So how should you apply it? Dr. King likes to gently rub or massage the powder into the scalp with her fingertips so that it’s not visible, she says.

The only downside? There is only one shade available: Translucent. It hasn’t left my caramel complexion looking ghostly. However, the brand makes other tinted powder sunscreens. I’d appreciate it if this SPF 50 became available in richer shades to accommodate more melanin-rich complexions and anyone with dark hair like mine.

Although it’s expensive, associate style and reviews editor Shannen Zitz has repurchased this sunscreen for over three years. ColoreScience is the only tinted sunscreen Zitz found that matches her cool-toned fair complexion without leaning too warm or too dark. “Tinted or non-tinted, it’s one of the only sunscreens that doesn’t cause acne—and I’m on Accutane—and it feels really nice on my skin,” she says.

Men’s Health associate health and fitness editor Jocelyn Solis-Moreira found success with the shade Medium. She admits being picky about sunscreens and often stocks up on European and Asian brands when traveling because those typically don’t leave behind a dreaded whitecast. However, ColoreScience impressed her after one try.

“With only a pea-sized amount, I saw an immediate difference in my face,” she says. It helped brighten her complexion, masked redness on her nose, and even had friends complimenting her glow. “It honestly felt like a layer of foundation that blended perfectly into my tan skin,” she says. She was so delighted with the results that she didn’t even apply concealer or setting powder. “I had to honestly do a double-take the first time that I was applying sunscreen and not makeup,” she says. “I would 100% recommend this product and will be a regular customer after this experience.”

Colbert was impressed by the lightweight texture but noted it required more effort to use. Notably, she had to wait for it to transform from white to her rich complexion before blending it onto her face. Colbert admits she had to work the sunscreen into her skin to ensure it didn’t look streaky, and that she didn’t miss any spots while waiting for the color to change. Still, she appreciates the overall appearance it left on her complexion. While not her perfect shade match, rich does resemble how her skin looks after a beach vacation.

Although each shade adapts to your complexion, I passed on this one because the limited color range wasn't a good fit for my olive undertones. Still, given the multiple rave reviews from our staff, it’s worth trying if you have the extra funds.

The world of sunscreen can sometimes feel like a catch-22: Either you're stuck using SPF that imparts a gnarly white cast, or you're using one that leaves your skin irritated and sensitive. The Supergoop! PLAY Everyday Lotion with SPF 50 sidesteps both of those issues, according to editorial assistant Katie Mogg. “The lightweight formula melts into my skin seamlessly, all while making it feel hydrated and nourished,” she says. Plus, it offers 80 minutes of water resistance, making it her go-to SPF for my sweaty outdoor running sessions.

Although I prefer a tinted face sunscreen, when I know I’ll be near the water or exercising outdoors I opt for this SPF. Play Everyday is my beach bag essential and for any trips to the park. It absorbs quickly without leaving behind a sticky residue on my body. Supergoop! doesn’t leave behind an ashy finish either. Instead, it blends flawlessly into my complexion.

The only thing I’d change about this sunscreen is the sizing options. There are four sizes, the most of any recommendations this list. However, only the extra large 18 fl. oz bottle comes with a pump. It would be nice to have the flexability of a pump with the other sizes, or at least the standard. But it’s not a true deal breaker, and I still like how slim the original squeeze bottle of sunscreen is and how it doesn’t take up too much space in my checked suitcase and beach bag.

Supergoop! is a favorite among dermatologists and our editors for its super-clear formulas—and rightfully so! This all-over version of the brand's star product—the Unseen Sunscreen SPF 40—does the same thing its predecessor does: it goes on invisible, feels velvety and weightless, and offers out-of-this-world sun protection.

"So many sunscreens have given my skin this heavy, greasy feeling right after I apply them, and on a really hot day in the sun, sometimes that can make you feel even hotter," says beauty contributor Danielle Jackson. "This formula is so light that I almost forgot I even had it on. It really makes you feel like you're not wearing anything."

Aloian has oily skin and easily breaks out, but she didn’t experience any body acne with this SPF. She didn't layer it with other body products, but she was impressed by how easily it spread, thanks to its more liquid texture, which blends into her sensitive areas like the neck. “I love this sunscreen—it doesn't leave any white streaks or irritate my skin. It'll definitely stay in my skincare routine for the long haul,” she says.

Honestly, the only con with this sunscreen is that it’s slightly pricey. However, we’ve been testing this SPF for over a month, and our editors predict each container will last them two to three months before a restock.

Ultraviolet radiation from the sun falls into two categories: ultraviolet A (UVA) and ultraviolet B (UVB). UVA rays cause signs of aging, such as hyperpigmentation, lines, and wrinkles. Meanwhile, UVB rays can cause more serious damage, including sunburn and skin cancer. Your safest bet is to only use broad-spectrum sunscreens to help protect against UVA and UVB rays.

Next, choose either a mineral or a chemical sunscreen. Here’s more insight to help you determine between the two formulations.

They both have benefits and limitations, but ultimately, the best one is the sunscreen you’ll actually use and reapply. As for me? Well, I like both types. However, I typically use mineral sunscreen on my face, so I can head outside immediately after work instead of lingering for the approximately 15-minute waiting period associated with chemical sunscreens.

Broad-spectrum coverage, sunscreen type, and SPF coverage are the big three considerations. But another factor worth emphasizing is other non-active skincare ingredients that will help bolster your complexion. Dermatologist Elyse Love, MD, is a big fan of niacinamide to calm the skin and improve its tone and texture. Also, look for ingredients that support your skin type and goals. For example, if you want to brighten your complexion, you'll look for a sunscreen with vitamin C. If you have dry skin, seek out hydrating ingredients like hyaluronic acid.

When we initially published this story in May 2019, it was a gallery featuring a handful of sunscreens. Nearly seven years later, we’ve seriously upgraded our product vetting process.

For starters, we polled dermatologists about the actual sunscreens they use IRL and recommend to patients. The doctors answered a series of questions about the efficacy, application, and real-world testing experience that helped inform their suggestions.

Next, I evaluated the hundreds of sunscreens in the Women’s Health beauty closet. I also polled Women’s Health and Men’s Health editors about their ride-or-die sunscreens. Our team varies across age, skin type, complexion, budget, and lifestyle. For example, fitness editor Cori Ritchey, CSCS, is a certified strength and conditioning coach and group fitness instructor. She has a no-frills approach to beauty and wants a simple sunscreen that delivers results, which she found in La Roche-Posay.

Clear sunscreens were carefully evaluated. Our team asked ourselves if the clear sunscreens squeezed out clear or were they white or creamy and then blended out without a trace? Associate health and fitness editor Addison Aloian and editorial assistant Katie Mogg found success with Supergoop!

Tinted sunscreens were also inspected because I know firsthand what it’s like to try and find your best color match only for it to look ruddy or cool in natural sunlight. With 17 flexible shades, Tower 28 delivers the most inclusive range among the sunscreens we vetted. The hues vary in depth and undertone, and offer light-to-medium coverage.

Whether you have oily, dry, or combination skin, there's something on our list for you. Meet our team’s all-time favorite sunscreens that we’ll continue to rely on throughout 2026.

You’ll want to keep an eye out for certain key phrases on the label. Dealing with sensitive skin? Dermatologist Marnie Nussbaum, MD, recommends fragrance-free and hypoallergenic formulas. She also prefers mineral sunscreens made with zinc oxide or titanium dioxide for sensitive skin because they’re less likely to cause irritation. Acne happens to the best of us, but your best path forward is to use an oil-free and non-comedogenic sunscreen that won’t congest your pores.

#4860. How Dwight Howard Built His ‘Superman’ Physique

The NBA center talks training, injuries, and discipline.

MORE THAN OTHER pro athletes, NBA players tend to enter their professional careers as skinny kids, still developing out of high school. To a degree, that’s exactly what happened with Dwight Howard, the first pick of the 2004 NBA draft. “My first year in the league, I got kind of pushed around,” Howard said on MH’s Strong Talk. “I didn’t like it.” Howard spent that offseason “eating weights” and became on the most muscular (and dominant) players ever. He earned the nickname “Superman” and went on to a Hall of Fame career. For almost two decades, Howard played for multiple teams and won an NBA championship with the Los Angeles Lakers in 2020.

Howard’s superhero physique came from more than shooting hoops. The center began building a disciplined training regimen as a high schooler, waking up at 4 a.m. to run track and hit the weight room.

“I told my dad at 10 I wanted to go to the NBA, and he said, ‘Well, you got to learn how to sacrifice now. You know your time and your effort. You have to learn how to be disciplined,’” Howard says in the latest Strong Talk episode.

Howard took his dad’s words to heart, already having the foresight that establishing a routine now would be easier than breaking bad training habits upon entering the NBA. His training over the years has evolved into different fitness challenges: from training in high-altitude terrains in Aspen to taking on Pilates and yoga.

Speaking with MH fitness director Ebenezer Samuel, C.S.C.S. and exercise physiologist and strength coach Dr. Pat Davidson, Howard goes into detail about the strength exercises he did to stay fit during the season, what he’s learned from trying to play through injuries, and the upcoming launch of the Rize Above with Dwight app next month that will offer fitness guidance to individuals of any age starting a fitness journey.

But it’s much more than a way to display finger foods. Often situated in a central location at a party, a cheese board works as a decorative design piece, and when done well, can even be a conversation starter. In fact, some boards themselves read as a still life, even after half the Brie is gone.

The most unique cheese boards combine material and shape, offering something distinct and memorable to house the bites (or function as a surface for slicing a baguette). Designers are creating beautiful centerpieces by carving wood into soft, stonelike forms or cutting marble into asymmetrical ovals. Ahead, find seven cheese boards to invest in now, each one pretty enough to steal the spotlight at any event.

Sarah Sherman Samuel is known for blending character with clean modern lines in her interiors, and her cheese board trio for Lulu and Georgia brings that same sensibility to the table. The set includes two marble boards and one made of acacia, allowing you to layer textures; situating soft cheeses on cool stone and bread on wood. The three sizes allow you to extend your spread down a long table for a crowd or cuddle everything close on the counter.

These amorphous-shaped boards by Danish brand Ferm Living are inspired by cairns, the stacks of stones that hikers leave as markers on the trail. Each is carved from solid ash that’s certified by the FSC—a third-party organization that confirms responsible sourcing of wood—and is given a carbonized finish that turns the wood a deep espresso shade. When you’re not using the boards to display cheese, you can stack them on a counter where they’ll look like a sculptural piece.

For a more artful approach to your cheese board, check out this tortoiseshell option from CB2. Portuguese artisans hand-finish each piece in a reactive glaze, so no two boards come out identical. The amber and chocolate swirls highlight both white cheeses and green accoutrements, such as green grapes and Granny Smith apples, for an especially striking display. And at roughly 10 by 18 inches, the long board runs neatly down the center of a table.

Serena & Lily has made this wave shape its signature, commonly appearing on its crested mirrors and nightstands, and this board brings that coastal edge to the table. The scalloped surface is the relaxed, beach-house counterpoint to the more architectural boards on this list. At 18 inches, the small size suits a cozy night in for two, while the large, 30-inch board option has room to house a full spread with all the accoutrements.

Red marble has been having a moment, showing up on bathroom vanities and living room floors. This tray is a low-lift way to incorporate the material in your space. Cut from deep red stone into a sleek oval with a thick rim, the color of this CB2 cheese board is inherently festive but will look elevated and at home in your kitchen year-round. Because it’s solid marble, the veining and color will vary from tray to tray.

At 13 by 18.5 inches, the generously sized Romie has room for the full spread, with space for several cheeses, cured meats, a cluster of grapes, and a stack of crackers that won’t slide off the edge. Its classic oval shape is made from acacia that’s stained a deep chocolate, bringing out the grain and hiding knife marks. It’s an Anthropologie exclusive and a beautiful board to reach for when you’re feeding more than a few people.

The artist Neil Cohen designed this 15-inch acacia block for the New Mexico–based brand Nambe, and the piece’s best feature is hidden in plain sight. The wood is carved with nooks that hold the knife and spreader flush with the surface, so the tools stay with the board instead of getting lost in a drawer, which is a pretty great feature. The clean shape is modern, making it an easy hostess gift.

#4857. The 8 Best Slippers for Women for Max Coziness, Tested By a Style Writer

From couch-rotting to errands, these kicks have you covered.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

Now that the weather has cooled down and leaves are on the ground, my style writer brain is in peak outfit mode. I’ve already imagined the ways I’ll wear my leather jackets, chunky knits, and bootcut jeans. But before I start styling my way through the fall and winter, there’s one essential I always reach for first: slippers. I test a lot of shoes in the name of journalism, and few spark more joy than a pair of cute slippers that add the perfect cozy feel to any outfit. Whether I’m channeling my inner couch potato on a lazy Sunday or running errands around town, the best slippers in my stash hit the sweet spot of soft, supportive, and actually stylish.

A lot of the same principles that apply to shopping for supportive sneakers also apply to slippers, says Anne Sharkey, DPM, a podiatrist at Solely Podiatry in Austin, TX. After all, a slipper is the ultimate cozy shoe, but it’s also incredibly useful for keeping your arches happy while walking around hardwood floors at home. That’s why Sharkey says cushioning and arch support are key. Your slippers should feel plush underfoot, but not so squishy that you lose stability. Where you plan to wear them also matters: A pair of house slippers needs less traction and durability than a pair for outdoors, which should have a thicker, more grippy bottom.

After over a year of testing, I found slippers that are plush enough to lounge in, supportive enough for a spin around town, and stylish enough that you’ll actually want to wear them.

When it comes to a slipper that checks every box (plush, supportive, and legitimately stylish), the Ugg Cozy Slipper is the one I always come back to. I’ve been wearing this slipper since fall 2024 with everything from jeans and Henleys to matching sweat sets.

The slipper earns its name with extra-cozy materials, from the sheepskin fur lining to the sweater-knit outer and fluffy collar. I love that it keeps my feet warm and toasty, even during cold winter months. Board-certified foot and ankle surgeon Bobby Pourizaee, DPM says this slipper is excellent for comfort and lounging. Podiatrist and board-certified foot and ankle surgeon Bruce Pinker, DPM agrees, adding that the slip-on style makes this slipper easy to wear.

Beneath the fluff, there’s real structure that keeps my feet fatigue-free. The contoured footbed and firm-yet-plush midsole made with 17 mm of sheepskin hug my arches just right. The outsole is sturdy and grippy, made with dense EVA foam and tons of traction. I wear it on long walks with my dog around the Long Island suburbs and never worry about slipping or falling, no matter the weather. However, it’s still lightweight enough to feel like an indoor slipper.

Pinker says that it could be improved if the heel region were closed for more support and stability, but the easy-on, easy-off fit is part of why I love this slipper. If you’re after something warm, cozy, and super stylish for both indoor and outdoor wear, I can’t recommend this slipper enough.

For a cozy, budget-friendly slipper that doesn’t skimp on comfort, the Dearfoams Lacey Memory Foam Slipper is the one I’ve been living in lately. At under $30, this slipper is way more cushy, warm, and supportive than lots of other house slippers I’ve worn.

I padded around my house in this slipper nonstop for about a year, and it held up beautifully through coffee runs to the kitchen, long hours at my desk, and quick trips to grab packages. It’s definitely a house slipper, but in the best way possible—pure comfort, with just enough structure to feel supportive.

The memory foam cushioning is what makes this slipper so comfortable, Sharkey says. Each step in it feels super plush, molding to the shape of my foot for that “walking on pillows” feel. The fleece lining also keeps my feet cozy without overheating, and the soft knit upper gives it a lounge-all-day kind of vibe that pairs perfectly with pajamas and sweatpants. I absolutely love the heel and arch cushioning, especially when my feet ache after a long day commuting to and from Manhattan, but Sharkey says they should only be worn in the house since they lack the structure needed for long periods on your feet.

But for a house slipper, there’s way more support than I expected. The raised heel area keeps the slipper from sliding off my foot, even when I’m walking up or down stairs. It’s a small but thoughtful feature that makes it feel a bit more secure than your average slip-on. And while the outsole isn’t meant for outdoor adventures, it’s durable enough for quick steps onto the porch or grabbing the mail.

I wore this slipper for nearly a year straight while trodding around my house, and absolutely love them. However, I will say that at about the 10-month mark, they needed to be replaced, as they stretched out a bit and lost some of the much-needed cushioning, support, and traction.

Thanks to its incredible level of cushioning, the Vionic Gemma II Mule Slipper keeps my feet pain-free even after walking in it all day. Pourizaee says it's a strong recommendation thanks to the contoured footbed. The midsole is made from a flexible EVA foam that not only feels super plush under my foot but is designed to absorb shock and reduce stress on the joints. I have lingering ankle and foot pain on one side from a previous high ankle sprain, and while some shoes exacerbate those symptoms, this slipper keeps my feet happy. That comes as no surprise, since this slipper earned an APMA Seal of Acceptance.

It also has great support and stability features. Pinker says it would be improved with a closed-heel design, but I find that the deep heel cup helps, and the strap closure keeps my foot firmly planted—even while speed walking on city sidewalks. Pourizaee adds that the contoured footbed helps keep feet aligned and relieves foot strain. While I often wake up with sore feet that hurt as soon as I step out of bed, I find that when I’ve worn this slipper the day before, foot fatigue is next to zero.

If you like a cozy slipper, the Gemma II delivers. I have the cream color, which is made with a wool upper that keeps my feet warm and looks cute with all my cold-weather loungewear. Other styles have a faux-fur or flannel upper, which also looks super warm and cozy. Plus, since the slipper is designed for indoor and outdoor wear, the synthetic outsole is ultra-durable with a patterned tread design. I’ve even gone for post-rain walks with my dog on wet pavement, and never felt like I was going to slip.

Overall, this slipper is warm, cozy, and ultra-cushioned. It keeps my feet happy with the plush feel underfoot, and I love keeping it by the door when I need a cute shoe to slip on fast.

If you need a slipper with serious arch support, the Orthofeet Charlotte Slipper delivers. Plus, it comes with additional insoles and spacers for days when my feet need extra support.

The Ortho-Cushion system (which includes the removable orthotic insole, ergonomic sole, and fitting spacers) helps to customize the fit and level of cushioning and support. I didn’t realize before selecting my normal size that Orthofeet recommends ordering a half-size down for a more snug fit, but placing the smallest blue fitting spacer (1/16 inch) under the insole kept my foot feeling super secure. Even without any customization, I was impressed by the high level of cushioning that hugs my arches and feels really nice under my heels. The ergonomic sole not only has ample cushioning underfoot, but also the subtle “rocker” design, which refers to a little lift under the heel and toe so those two parts of the shoe don’t touch the ground when standing still, similar to a rocking chair. That shape propels you forward with each step and also helps take some pressure off the joints. Plus, the EVA outsole also has lots of traction patterns to keep every step feeling stable and secure.

I also love the faux fur lining and insole that feels super cozy and keeps my feet warm even while walking outdoors on chilly mornings. The suede outer adds to that cozy vibe and looks super cute. I initially wasn’t sure if this slipper would be my style, but I find myself reaching for it all the time when I leave the house for quick errands and coffee dates with friends. I have the taupe color and often pair it with ankle jeans and sweaters for a comfortable fall fit.

While it does run slightly small, the brand offers half sizes, and the slipper comes with customizable features, so I didn’t find it an issue at all. However, if you’re concerned about fit, I recommend ordering a half size down.

The Sunday Mule Slipper from Bombas is perhaps the most stylish casual shoe that I own. The elongated, oval-toe shape looks super chic, and it's wrapped entirely in a fluffy sherpa material for that cozy-yet-put-together feel. Whether I’m couch-rotting on the weekend, grabbing a latte, or taking a casual stroll around town, I can always count on this slipper. It looks great with a wide-leg lounge pant or leggings with slouchy socks, but I’ve also worn it with a cropped pair of jeans.

Sharkey says it's a good cozy and comfortable option, and that Bombas did a great job with the level of cushioning. That’s thanks to the memory foam footbed, which has a nice squishy feel, contours to the shape of the foot, and softens impact with every step. That contouring feature does wonders for making sure the slipper stays on, even while trekking all around town. However, Sharkey says the backless design does tend to slip off the feet if you’re not careful. I haven’t had any issues there, but it’s something to keep in mind if your feet need an ultra-supportive shoe—in which case, the Orthofeet Charlotte Slipper might be a better choice.

The rubber outsole gives this slip-on shoe a major upgrade, since it helps provide traction when I wear it outside. I keep this slipper mainly for wearing around the house or quick errands, but I have worn it during short, casual walks without worry. The fluffy sherpa material, inside and out, makes it a super cozy option for lazy days cuddled up on the couch and keeps my feet warm even when I take it for a spin outdoors.

Plus, there’s plenty of chic color options. I went with the cream, which I find pairs well with almost anything in my closet—but there’s also a black and brown for additional neutrals, and a dusty purple or tomato red option for something more bold. While this slipper from Bombas might not be the most supportive option, I’d recommend it to anyone looking for a plush, super stylish slipper.

Clogs get a bad rap for making your feet sweat, slide around, and (sorry!) being kind of ugly. But this slip-on clog from Rothy’s nails it on the style front, and is also durable, breathable, and super comfortable. The Casual Clog is well-loved by me and executive editor Abigail Cuffey—oh, and Sharkey recommends it, too.

This slipper/clog hybrid is made with the brand’s signature cushioning made from recycled water bottles and arch support that Sharkey says is ultra comfortable. She also says she likes that the heel cup is a bit deeper than your standard slipper, which helps with stability. I find that the deep heel cup helps cover the back of my foot, so it doesn’t slip off when I’m running around the house doing laundry or walking up and down stairs. The outsole is also made from recycled water bottles and has a grooved design that makes it super durable with tons of traction. I usually wear it for casual outings and meeting up with friends, and find it looks great with baggy jeans and sweaters for a casual-yet-put-together look.

While I own the merino wool version, Cuffey owns both the merino wool and hemp styles. She’s been wearing the hemp clog since fall 2024, and loves that the ultra-cushioned footbed molds to her feet. “It feels like a hug for your heels and toes,” she says. She wears it as a lounge shoe and an outdoor shoe, because of the grippy outsole and substantial feel. Cuffey’s thoughts on the merino wool clog are generally the same, but she loves that the wool feels a little cozier while still airy and breathable. “I usually go through slippers so fast because they get so gross, but Rothy’s Casual Clogs are the first ones that have staying power in my closet,” she says.

It does run a little wide, but the fabric is stretchy, so I haven’t had any issues with it feeling too loose on my feet. But if you’re in between sizes, Rothy’s recommends sizing down for a better fit.

The L.L. Bean Wicked Good Moccasin has become my favorite ever since I got it in the mail. A moccasin is a slipper made of soft leather that wraps around the foot with a single gathered seam at the front. This style is the cushiest, coziest, most supportive I’ve ever worn, earning a permanent spot in my fall and winter footwear rotation.

Unlike some moccasins, Pinker says this style feels especially stable thanks to the rubber outsole with added grip and traction. Plus, the suede material is more structured than other moccasins I’ve worn, which makes for a snug, secure feel. I’ve worn this moccasin weekly over the past month, and I can tell it’s extremely durable. The suede has a lot of heft, and combined with the hand-stitched construction, this moccasin stands up to wear and tear. The fur lining is also extremely comfortable and warm, and I love wearing this shoe on colder days to keep my feet toasty. The insole is also made from the same fur material, which delivers a super plush, cushioned feel underfoot.

There’s also plenty of fur lining the outside of the slipper, which I find super stylish, along with the rawhide laces and bow. It looks great with both joggers and wide-leg sweatpants, and I even wore it recently with cuffed jeans and a boxy sweater for a casual brunch. I have the brown pair, but with seven shades to choose from (including blue, red, and purple!), there’s no shortage of styling potential.

One note: this slipper is spot-clean only, unlike others that can go in the washing machine. However, I wear it nearly every morning lately to walk my dog when the ground is still dewy, and I haven’t gotten any stains that took more than a quick pass with a dry washcloth to remove.

I desperately needed a new house slipper a few weeks ago, so I decided to snag this pair from Fulton—and I couldn’t be happier with my decision. While you could totally get away with wearing this slipper outside (it’s super cute and definitely sturdy), I love keeping this pair inside and free from outside germs—IYKYK.

At first, I honestly wasn’t sure this pair would be a winner: the footbed was super uncomfortable the first day that I wore them. It felt like all the raised areas were in the wrong places, which made it a little difficult to walk. Had I known then that the Fulton website explains there’s a 10-hour break-in process, I’d have been way less concerned.

Lo and behold, by the following day the slippers felt much better—and only continued to get more comfortable as the cork footbed molded to the exact shape of my foot. I wouldn’t call this slipper plush by any means (though the wool upper is quite cozy), so if that’s what you’re looking for, the Ugg, Dearfoams, Orthofeet, or L.L. Bean styles might be better options. But this shoe makes my feet feel so good.

I’ve been suffering from some pretty gnarly foot pain from recently developed plantar fasciitis, but since I started wearing this slipper around the house every day, my feet feel brand new. My arches and heels feel way less achy throughout the day, and it no longer hurts to plant my feet on the ground first thing in the morning.

If you prefer a slide over a slipper, this pick from Oofos is perfect. I often bring it to the gym to wear in the locker room, sauna, or on the way to my post-workout smoothie spot, and the cushy foam insole feels great on my achy feet. As our WH 2025 Fitness Awards winner for Best Recovery Shoe, I had to test it myself for this guide.

Pourizaee says this slide is ideal for recovery or all-day wear thanks to its excellent shock absorption and built-in arch support. That’s because it’s made from the brand's signature OOfoam technology—a springy EVA foam that has plenty of cushion and feels nice and squishy underfoot. The insole’s contoured shape creates built-in arch support, with a high mound near the center that fits perfectly under the arches. That shape reduces stress on the knees, ankles, and other joints. My ankle pain (from a previous sprain) and mysterious knee pain definitely feel better when I wear this slide regularly around the house. Plus, the deep heel cup keeps my foot anchored in place, even when I’m doing housework at lightning speed.

WH executive health and fitness director, Jacqueline Andriakos, swears by it for managing her foot pain, too. "My podiatrist told me I had to get a pair for work-from-home days and going to and from barefoot workout classes," she says. "I notice my chronic foot pain is light years better when I’ve been wearing it more regularly."

Another perk? The foam is water-repellent, odor-resistant, and machine washable. The only feature that would make this slide better, Pinker says, is an ankle strap for extra stability and support.

The right cushioning absorbs impact from walking on hard surfaces to help prevent foot pain, says Pourziaee. All of our favorite slippers have at least a medium level of cushioning.

The support features in any shoe, especially a slipper, are some of the most important aspects to consider. Experts say to examine the following:

I’m a shopping writer covering style for Women’s Health. I’ve written guides to the best white t-shirts, most comfortable sneakers, best walking shoes, and more. I also test footwear (including slippers and slides!) constantly.

When I first wrote the story in November 2025, I personally tested over 20 popular styles, pulling favorites from my closet and trying new pairs. For over four months, I wore those slippers at least two to three times per week for full days at a time.

Since then, I’ve continued to put the originally tested slippers through their paces, wearing some pairs on long walks with my dog around Long Island and even commuting to work in Manhattan in a few styles to see how they held up to my daily 10,000-step-count goal.

I also reached out to three podiatrists for their insights on the best features and materials to look for, and I received their honest thoughts on my top picks. #4856. The Best Hoodies for Men, Tested by Style Editors

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

We recommend options from Alo and Champion.

AS A MEN’S HEALTH style editor, I spend most of my office days wearing business-casual and semi-dressy fits. But when I clock out, I have a closet stacked with hoodies that I love to slip on. From freezing winters in New Jersey during my teen years to long days on campus at Howard University, they’ve always been a core piece in my wardrobe. Thankfully, hoodies have come a long way since then—gone are the days of big, boxy sweats that make you disappear into your clothes. Today, the best hoodies for men aren’t just better in fit, fabric, and function—they actually look good, too.

A hoodie is basically your favorite long-sleeve tee or crewneck—but with a hood attached. Pullovers give you that classic, laid-back vibe, while zip-up styles make it easy to throw on or peel off without messing up your hair. The best hoodies for men are made from soft, smooth fabrics like cotton or fleece that feel great on your skin, and some even come with moisture-wicking tech if you’re hitting the trails, the gym, or just dealing with unpredictable weather.

As Men’s Health editors, we practically live in sweats during the fall and winter, whether we’re heading to the gym, running errands, going on work trips, or curling up on the couch. Over the last five years, our team has tested countless options, from OG brands like Abercrombie and Champion to newer athleisure labels like Alo and Vuori. These are the hoodies that left a lasting impression—and are still in rotation.

In typical Alo fashion, the brand’s Accolade Hoodie nails that sweet spot between streetwear and luxury. From the chrome branding on the chest to the hefty cotton-polyester fabric that feels soft and substantial, it has that premium vibe you notice the second you pull it on. The french terry exterior has this plush, fuzzy texture that amps up its comfort factor and makes you want to lounge in it all day.

This one’s got a boxy, oversized cut that gives me full freedom to move how I want, whether I’m reaching overhead to grab a coffee mug and bending to tie my sneakers without the fabric pulling under the arms. Despite the larger relaxed fit, I don’t feel stuffy or like I’m swimming in fabric. Plus, it has an exceptional warmth-to-weight ratio, keeping me cozy without overheating during those weird in-between weather days. It's ideal for guys who prefer a looser feel, whether you're layering over a tee or a crewneck. If you prefer a slimmer fit, I’d recommend going down a size (or even two).

I’ve worn mine to grab breakfast in Soho and to and from workouts, and it always looks on point. While it comes in a bunch of slick tones, I’m especially into the rich brown. This color makes it feel a bit dressier than your average hoodie and on trend for fall, so I’m never shy about wearing it out in public.

When it comes to comfortable athleisure wear that you can sport almost every day, Lululemon churns out the best of the best. Take the brand's relaxed-fitting style hoodie, which doesn't feel too loose or baggy. We found there's plenty of room in the chest and at the waist, meaning you can easily layer long-sleeve T-shirts and still receive a great deal of breathability. Plus, the cotton-blend fabric has a hint of stretch, so it's perfect for guys with broader shoulders and bigger biceps.

Our style editors raved about how breathable the fabric is, making it a top option for all-day wear, from their workout class to the beer hall. Thanks to the brushed interior, you get that next-to-skin warmth that keeps you feeling toasty when the temps dip. Despite its steep price point, this fleece pullover can handle several washes and multiple seasons. We've worn it through the fall and into the spring—pairing it with chinos, jeans, and sweats.

And if you don't feel like carrying your backpack, the Steady State Hoodie comes with a wide kangaroo pouch, so there's a place to store your phone, wallet, beanie—or warm your hands.

Abercrombie’s hoodie is my go-to for travel days when all I care about is being comfortable on my flights. The fit runs a little oversized, but it doesn’t make you look like you’re wearing a puffy trash bag. You get extra room in the body and waist with the option to layer anything that’s slim-fitting or slightly bulky. If you like a closer fit, just size down.

I’ve had mine for a couple of years now, and the cotton-polyester fabric still feels as soft as the day I unboxed it. I’ve put it through countless washes, coffee spills, and lazy weekends, and yet the color and shape haven’t budged. I’ve also wore it during a chilly fall photoshoot and was impressed by how it held up against the wind better than half of the performance hoodies we tested.

Style-wise, it’s one of those hoodies that just works with anything—sweatpants, jeans, joggers, or even chino pants when you’re dressing up for casual Fridays. The washed finish gives it a vintage, lived-in vibe that looks polished, not sloppy. And while it skips the drawstring, I’ve never once wished it had one—the hood stays put even when the wind kicks up. The front pouch pocket is spacious enough to keep your hands warm on cold morning errand runs. Plus, this hoodie comes in an insane amount of colors to choose from.

When it comes to hoodies, Champion wrote the playbook. More than a decade after my college years, the brand’s still cranking out affordable sweats like this one that feel anything but cheap. The cotton-polyester blend is thick, soft, and surprisingly resilient, while the patented reverse weave technique (a unique manufacturing process) boosts its lifespan and reduces shrinking, wash after wash. After six washing cycles, the fabric held up nicely without becoming dingy or pilling. Compared to other hoodies that we've tested, this might be the heaviest option on the list, meaning you get all the cozy vibes without feeling weighed down.

The loose cut leaves room to layer over basics, and the hoodie stretches just enough for reaching, bending, or grabbing a coffee on the go. While it might be too warm for a cool summer night, it’s perfect for fall walks, weekend errands, or casual hangouts. Either way, it keeps you toasty during shoulder season without needing a fleece jacket. We also love how effortlessly it pairs with jeans, sweats, or relaxed trousers—making it a reliable, everyday hoodie that delivers serious quality without breaking the bank.

Cozy Earth’s hoodie has that sink-into-the-couch kind of comfort you get from the brand’s pajamas and sheets. It’s made from combed cotton and polyester, which is soft, supple, and weighted just right, giving it a drapey, almost cloud-like feel against the skin. Unlike Reigning Champ’s hoodie, which has a more structured build, Cozy Earth’s version feels more forgiving and relaxed like a wearable hug, perfect for lazy mornings in bed or weekend binge-watching sessions.

The subtle branding on the chest keeps the look minimal and versatile. Our editors note it has that weightless feel that makes you never want to take it off. Even without spandex, the hoodie lets us lift the suitcase into an overhead bin. Not to mention, its relaxed fit is perfect to layer underneath and wear on a flight as it tends to get cold on the aircraft. The inside has stayed plush wash after wash, while the outside keeps a smooth, lived-in softness that drapes neatly.

When the weather really goes rogue in the winter, Carhartt’s heavyweight hoodie might be your best defense. It’s seriously thick—built to take on wind, cold, and even a bit of drizzle, thanks to the durable water-repellent finish. Our editors noted how it shrugged off light rain on a walk to the gym without soaking through. Another editor wore it for a weekend cabin trip and said it kept him perfectly comfortable chopping wood outside in 40-degree weather. It feels insulated without weighing you down like a full-on parka. This is on brand for Carhartt, which specializes in producing durable workwear that can handle all sorts of conditions.

Instead of the hood being cut from one flat piece of fabric, it’s paneled to better contour to your head and neck, meaning it doesn’t bunch up or blow off when the wind picks up. The inside jersey lining feels soft like your favorite tee, and even with a beanie underneath the hood didn’t feel tight or floppy. Reclaimed warehouse beams from a similar time period to the original structures line the vaulted ceiling, with original iron bolts still in place.

#4852. Emideltide Keeps Getting a ‘No’ for Compounding. What’s the Problem?

Why the government’s renewed interest in peptides excludes this one.

THE TRUMP ADMINISTRATION has not been shy about its pro-peptide stance. US Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has pushed to make six popular yet unapproved peptides available for compounding to people with a prescription. A recent FDA advisory committee meeting voted in favor of adding six out of seven peptides to a list of substances that U.S. compounding pharmacies are allowed to manufacture and supply.

Six out of seven. So what happened to that last peptide? Emideltide, also dubbed DSIP, is a peptide people have turned to for better sleep. And it was the only peptide the FDA advisory board voted against moving out of the Category 2 list—a substance considered to carry significant safety risks, with compounding pharmacies prohibited from making it. Here’s why.

EMIDELTIDE IS A nine-amino-acid peptide originally isolated from the blood of sleeping rabbits during electrically induced sleep in the late 1970s. Since its discovery, a synthetic peptide version has been administered via injection or a nasal spray.

Emideltide reportedly helps you fall asleep faster and extend the time spent in deep sleep. It’s also been used to avoid waking up multiple times throughout the night and anecdotal reports online have mentioned more vivid, Inception–like lucid dreaming. With better sleep, people online using emideltide have mentioned feeling less stress, more refreshed upon waking, and faster recovery after a grueling workout.

MOST RESEARCH LOOKING into the peptide’s role in sleep, however, took place in the 1980s and 1990s—with mixed findings.

For example, a 1984 case study reported on a 35-year-old guy with 10 years of narcolepsy who had reduced sleep attacks, less daytime napping, and more alertness with weekly emideltide injections administered in the morning.

One clinical trial had 16 people take an emideltide injection or a placebo while measuring how long it took for them to fall asleep once they’re tucked into bed. People who had an emideltide injection said they felt more tired and actually went to sleep quicker than the placebo group. That should be great except when they repeated the experiment a second night, the placebo group knocked out quicker than the peptide group.

Another study in 1992 found the peptide helped chronic insomniacs feel less tired. However, there was such little difference in the time it took to fall asleep and stay asleep in the emideltide group versus the placebo group. The authors of the 1992 study said any small improvements with the peptide were probably “due to an incidental change in the placebo group” and “not likely to be of major therapeutic benefit.”

BEYOND SLEEP, EMIDELTIDE has been explored in animal studies for potentially protecting against cancer and improving motor ability after stroke. Another realm of interest is how emideltide might help with curbing withdrawal after addiction.

A 1984 study found emideltide injections helped reduce the severity of opioid withdrawal symptoms in 97 percent of people with addiction along with alcohol withdrawal symptoms in 87 percent of people with alcohol addiction. Although more peptide injections were needed in people with opiate addiction.

In 1998, researchers gave a single injection of emideltide to seven people with opioid dependence. While they reported improvements in opioid withdrawal, the team also noted “it remains an open question whether DSIP could be an effective alternative detoxification approach.” Some of the issues were the small sample size, lack of a placebo group for proper comparison, and that each person knew they were getting an emideltide injection. The lack of randomization makes it hard to say for sure that a treatment actually worked or if people subjectively felt better because they knew they were getting treatment.

WE KNOW EMIDELTIDE doesn’t act like a sedative that slows down the brain and body’s function. But how the peptide exactly works is still up for debate.

The peptide is often considered a sleep-regulator rather than a suppressant. We know emideltide doesn’t act like a sedative or sleeping pill that slows down the brain and body’s function. But how the peptide exactly works is still up for debate.

One possible mechanism is that the peptide increases delta-wave activity. These are your slowest brain waves at 0.5 to 4 Hz that are indicative of deep sleep. Deep sleep is linked to better memory, energy, and all that good stuff you get from a good night’s sleep. There may also be some neuroendocrine effects going on that could explain why people feel calm enough to pass out. A small study back in the ’80s injected a single dose of emideltide in 11 guys and found lower levels of ACTH, a hormone that stimulates your adrenal glands to release the stress hormone cortisol (though this mechanism has been disputed).

The FDA advisory meeting relied on studies that focused on emideltide’s cross-talk with the opioid system in the brain. While the peptide doesn’t directly interact with opioid receptors, evidence points to emideltide somehow being able to trigger the release of endorphins. This may also provide painkiller properties (which is why it’s been proposed as a way to suppress alcohol and opioid withdrawal syndrome).

EMIDELTIDE WILL PROBABLY stay banned—and found only through the sketchy gray market—because there’s not enough information to know if emideltide might do more harm than good.

Since emideltide interacts with the opioid system, there is a possibility that it could lead to addiction. Right now, there are no animal or human studies that prove emideltide wouldn’t worsen addictive behaviors.

There’s also not enough data on whether repeated emideltide use would cause other safety issues. While the small sleep trials did not report any serious side effects, withdrawal studies noted headaches, nausea, and vertigo. After the second injection, some had low blood pressure although the researchers also said it’s unclear whether those symptoms were because of the peptide or from withdrawal altogether.

#4851. WNBA Star Gabby Williams Found a Team That Asked What She Wanted. Then She Won a Championship

The 30-year-old shares her philosophy on work-life balance and how she keeps her body strong and healthy on a new episode of The Huddle.

WNBA superstar Gabby Williams is proof that hard work and persistence pay off. Drafted into the league in 2018 by the Chicago Sky, the 30-year-old has been slowly building her résumé ever since—both stateside and abroad—notching her first EuroLeague championship in 2022 with Hungary’s Sopron Basket, being named a WNBA All-Star in 2025, and, finally, winning a WNBA Championship in 2026 with the Golden State Valkyries. (She was named Finals MVP too.)

Yes, 2026 has been a big year for the forward, and she has only a couple more months to rest up before taking on her next challenge: debuting in the Unrivaled league, as part of the Miami-based Laces BC.

“It's three-on-three, so you can't hide,” Gabby tells editors Abigail Cuffey, Amanda Lucci, and Jacqueline Andriakos on the latest episode of The Huddle. “The positive feedback that I've heard from people who have done it, [is] that the personal development side is great. Players usually go on to have great W seasons after doing Unrivaled.”

How could Gabby possibly top this past year!? We’ll have to wait to find out, but in the meantime, she opens up about finding a home with the Valkyries, keeping herself healthy and injury-free, and building a life outside of basketball.

Over the years, Gabby has earned the nickname “the French Army knife,” due not only to her dual-citizenship (her dad is American; her mom is French) but also to her versatility on the court.

Her role on many teams has been defined by what the team needed, whether it was creating opportunities or defending the paint. But when she went into free agency and signed with the Valkyries earlier this year, it was the first time Gabby recalls someone in the league asking what she wanted to do.

“I was proud to do whatever the team needed,” Gabby says. “But it was nice to trust myself.” That trust—both in herself and from her team—has obviously paid off. Not only does Gabby say she feels more like herself than she ever has, but she has the championship (the Valkyries’ first) to show for it.

Given how little downtime Gabby takes—she often spends part of her off-season playing abroad—she’s crafted a wellness routine that prioritizes stretching, mobility, and maintenance to keep her body in peak physical condition.

And it starts first thing when she wakes up. “I'm a big foam-roller stretcher, especially as I'm getting older,” she says. “I'll spend a good like 20, 15 minutes first thing in the morning just doing my mobility stuff so that when I come to the gym my body's awake and ready.”

At the gym, Gabby and her trainers prioritize accessory work over big Olympic lifts, to limit the wear and tear on her body.

In the off-season, Gabby shifts from a maintenance mindset to an improvement focus with her workouts. If she wants to strengthen a particular body part or movement pattern (like being more explosive) this is when she has the time and energy to do it.

No matter her training regimen, Gabby ends her day much like she starts it—with recovery. She loves an epsom salt bath and can’t get enough of her Normatec compression therapy.

It might be surprising to hear a WNBA champion say “basketball is not life,” but that’s precisely Gabby’s philosophy when it comes to balancing her priorities.

“I think that's why I've been able to have so much success in basketball is because I've learned how to compartmentalize,” she says. She credits that mindset to the coaching team at the University of Connecticut, where she played in college.

“Coach said, ‘When you're on the court, I want you to be focused. I don't want you to be thinking about school. I don't want you to be thinking about your personal life. So while you're doing your other stuff, don't focus on basketball as much. Find the time for your school. When you're going out, go out, have fun.’”

And so Gabby does just that, whether it’s solving a puzzle or picking up a new book. “It is just the perfect way to consume your mind with something else,” she says of reading. She’s even started a Valkyries book club, but it got a bit sidetracked by, of all things, the playoffs. Luckily, there’s always the 2027 season to start anew.

To hear more from Gabby, including her undying love of figure skating and how she’s upped her style game, click play on the latest episode of The Huddle above.

Hay’s line of furniture is an all-time AD favorite, so why not continue your love for the Danish brand by adding this soft-gray laundry bin with geometric lines into your design repertoire. It’s also narrow enough to fit tight spaces.

#4849. The 9 Best Sweaters for Men, Tested by Style Editors

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

From classic cotton crews to cozy cashmere, every knit is here.

I’LL ADMIT IT: sweaters are my kryptonite. Long before I was a style editor, they were my secret weapon. In my early twenties, I realized that a well-cut knit could elevate a look more effortlessly than any blazer or jacket. I’ve worn them through newsroom winters, weekend getaways, and way too many cold subway commutes to count. Growing up, I’d watch Pharrell Williams turn a simple crewneck into a statement, marvel at Andre 3000’s fearless layering, and admire A$AP Rocky’s ability to make a chunky sweater feel cool. Those moments have stuck with me, teaching me that style isn’t about what you wear but how you wear it. Sweaters became my canvas—and they still are, whether I’m braving the elements or dressing to impress.

Since 2020, the Men’s Health style team and I have tested more than 50 styles—crewnecks, cable knits, turtlenecks—to find the ones that actually deliver. Sweaters are also one of my go-to holiday gifts since they’re practical and available at just about every price point. Ahead, you’ll find our top picks that check every box, whether you’re shopping for yourself or grabbing dad a new knit for the season.

I’ve been testing men’s sweaters since 2020, so as you can imagine, I’ve worn more than I can count. Polo Ralph Lauren’s cable-knit has consistently risen above the competition in construction, fit, and timeless style. The brand helped cement the cable-knit as an American preppy classic, and that history shows in the sweater itself. The textured braids and patterns give it depth and richness, elevating even the simplest outfit. You can see and feel the heritage in every stitch—the weight, the structure, the classic lines all signal a piece built to last.

The relaxed fit is a major win for comfort—it offers extra room in the chest, which is perfect if you’ve got bigger pecs (like me, after a few years of lifting). Even without spandex, it layers beautifully over a button-up without stretching out or losing its shape. During testing, I wore it over a crisp white dress shirt for a dinner party, under a blazer for a Zoom meeting, and casually with joggers on a morning matcha latte run. The fabric feels soft against the skin but maintains structure. It never made me break a sweat, and kept me cozy in temps in the high 50s. I’ve washed mine over six times, and the sweater still looks and fits like new.

I also love how it pairs seamlessly with a variety of pants—tailored trousers, jeans, and casual sweats all work. And of course, that unmistakable Ralph Lauren heritage baked in, giving a sense of legacy that many sweaters lack. One thing to keep in mind: it comes with a premium price tag, which might be a barrier, only if you’re looking for a budget-friendly option that won’t exude as much style.

Amazon Essentials offers everything from the best men’s basics to sharp sweaters, and this one’s proof that affordable doesn’t mean cheaply made. This V-neck style is breathable in the winter, easy to layer, and feels surprisingly premium for the price. Our editors wore it under blazers and sport coats, and then over a crisp shirt with the collar peeking. (Don’t wear it with a T-shirt unless you’re going for a laid-back look). The regular fit is relaxed–but-not-boxy, and forgiving if you’ve just had a burger.

The 100 percent cotton knit feels soft against the skin with just the right amount of stretch, so there’s no restriction when I raise my arms or reach for my coffee. Given its price, you’d think it would become dingy after a few wears or washes, but that’s not the case. Despite months of wear and multiple wash cycles, it held its shape without fading or pilling. Bonus: it comes in a range of colors and argyle prints, so you can stock up and keep your office fits in rotation.

If outdoor running is part of your winter routine, you should consider Vuori’s Performance Crew. It’s designed with both comfort and functionality in mind. Made from a stretchy, moisture-wicking fabric, it keeps you dry and moves with you, whether you’re running errands or working up a sweat. The brand’s signature DreamKnit fabric feels like velvet and won’t overheat you when layered over a lightweight T-shirt or tank top. It's by far the smoothest, most buttery-soft fabric we’ve ever tested. With a modern athletic fit, the cut follows the natural shape of your body without being too tight or loose. You still have the freedom of movement while still looking put-together, so it’s perfect for intense workouts and casual wear.

A good cashmere sweater feels like wrapping yourself in a cloud, and Naadam’s version is one that our style team can’t get enough of. The first time I pulled it on, I understood why: it’s ridiculously soft—way softer than regular wool so it feels amazing against my skin without any itching. It’s lightweight too, so you don’t overheat when the radiator’s on full blast, but still warm enough for windy commutes.

After a few wears, I noticed it never lost its shape and didn’t pill as fast as cheaper cashmere sweaters I’ve tested (a small miracle at this price). Keep in mind: cashmere is delicate, so this one requires more care than cotton or polyester sweaters. I’m also a fan of how many colors they offer, including cobalt and tangerine that really stand out without being loud. For guys with athletic builds, it’s the perfect cut. It skims your frame just right, showing off your shoulders and giving your biceps a little spotlight. Just note: sizes do run small, so if you’re between sizes, go up.

I’ve tested a bunch of budget knits, but this one from Uniqlo punches way above its price tag. The cotton-blend fabric feels soft straight out of the package and has a tight ribbed construction that keeps its shape after a dozen washes, and somehow still looks brand new. Although it doesn’t have the weight or the luxe feel of higher-end knits, I’ve worn this for months and found no fading, stretching, or weird pilling.

The synthetic blend gives it that smooth, premium hand-feel with a bit of stretch, so you can reach, twist, and move without feeling boxed in. I also love how the fit strikes that sweet spot between tailored and relaxed—it skims the body without clinging, which makes it look sharp enough for the office but laid-back enough for Sunday coffee runs. The ribbing on the collar keeps it in shape and adds a subtle texture, providing a durable and neat finish. And since it’s machine washable, you can toss it in with your regular laundry and forget about dry cleaning.

I’ve always loved turtleneck sweaters—they’re dressier and provide more coverage than your standard crewneck. But if you’re on the shorter or leaner side, a full turtleneck can sometimes feel like too much fabric stacked around your neck. Suitsupply’s roll neck solves that problem perfectly. It delivers the same refined look and warmth of a turtleneck, just with less bulk so you don’t need a scarf. I found it especially handy during the freezing winter mornings. The merino wool breathes surprisingly well, so I didn’t overheat when layering it under a blazer or waiting for the train in a muggy subway station.

You can skip a trip to the dry cleaners because the fabric is tough enough to handle a spin in the washer and come out looking sharp with zero shrinkage or sagging. Plus, it’s odor-resistant, so I stayed fresh from my morning commute through my evening dinner. What I love the most is the versatility. Thanks to its minimalistic look, I’ve layered it under everything from a bomber jacket for errands to a tailored suit for a fancy holiday party. Whether you’re going for laid-back or dress-to-impress, this turtleneck fits the bill perfectly. The slim fit is clean but not constricting—enough to streamline my upper body without being tight, and yes, it gives the pecs a nice little lift. Guys with bigger chests or arms may have to size up for a comfortable fit.

This ribbed crew is one of those pieces that just feels right from the first wear. It’s made from a richly textured cotton rib that gives it some real weight—thicker than your average knit but never stiff or bulky. The texture adds that broken-in look while the classic fit keeps things clean and flattering. It sits close to the body without squeezing you, which makes it great for guys with broader shoulders who want structure, and it gives slimmer builds a sharper, more defined shape. It drapes cleanly through the shoulders and arms, and has just enough give whether you’re layering it under a jacket or reaching for something on a shelf.

What really sets it apart from other sweaters is the feel—it’s got that hearty, hand-knit texture you usually only get from a vintage find, but it wears lighter and breathes better than heavy wool. After its first wash, the ribbing softened up so much we wanted to wear it three days in a row. The look lands somewhere between rugged fisherman and clean-cut. Yeah, it’s not cheap, but the rich construction, flattering fit, and durability make it worth the investment.

If you’re going to wear a sweater, make sure it’s in a classic color that won’t feel dated after one season. This style comes in a nice red or grey that are bold enough to stand out but not overwhelming that you’ll regret it in photos later. It plays well with dressier trousers for a dinner or intimate gathering. The unique ribbing along the sides, neckline, and hem gives it some nice texture, while the standard fit hits that sweet spot between relaxed and put-together. It might feel a bit boxy if you prefer a more tailored, close-to-the-body look.

The merino wool and nylon fabric blend feels sturdy but not stiff—it’s thick enough to keep you warm on chilly mornings but breathable once you’re indoors. One of our testers even wore it on a coffee run and didn’t break a sweat under a jacket. It’s got just the right amount of stretch too, so you can move around without feeling like you're trapped in a knit straitjacket. The vibe is rugged but still polished, which means it works just as well with jeans and clean sneakers, as well as with tailored trousers and loafers.

I’ve been wearing this cashmere quarter-zip from Quince for a few weeks now, and it’s one of those sweaters that makes you realize how nice cashmere can actually feel. The fisherman rib knit gives it real heft and structure, so it feels premium the second you pull it on. This one is made from Mongolian cashmere, which has longer, finer fibers, so it's ten times softer and more durable. You’re basically getting that luxury feel for a budget-friendly price point. It has a classic fit but is trim enough that it doesn’t bunch up when you sit or layer it under a coat or over a button-down.

I wore this during New York City’s shoulder season, and it regulated temperature really well. I never got hot walking to work or felt chilly when the office AC kicked on. The fabric breathes better than most wool sweaters I’ve tested, and it never got that itchy, fuzzy feeling that cashmere can sometimes pick up after a few wears. Plus, the quarter-zip collar gives it versatility, too: zipped up, it looks sharp for the office; unzipped, it leans casual for the weekend. You can choose from a range of easy-to-wear neutral tones; think navy, black, and charcoal, which all pair effortlessly with chinos or dark jeans.

Look for high-quality materials that ensure warmth, comfort, and longevity. By understanding what each fabric brings to the table, you can select the sweater that fits both your lifestyle and your wardrobe goals. Here’s a closer look at what you can expect from the most common options:

Cashmere is the gold standard for softness and luxury. It’s made from the undercoat of cashmere goats, resulting in an ultra-fine, buttery fabric. Expect it to feel lightweight yet warm, perfect for layering without adding bulk. Cashmere sweaters often have a higher price tag, but their timeless appeal and plush feel make them a worthwhile investment. Just remember: cashmere requires delicate care, like handwashing or dry cleaning, to maintain its softness.

Merino wool is a performance powerhouse. Derived from Merino sheep, this wool is fine, soft, and naturally moisture-wicking, making it ideal for regulating body temperature. Merino wool sweaters keep you warm without overheating and are often odor-resistant, so they’re great for active or travel-heavy lifestyles. Bonus: Many are machine washable, adding a dose of convenience.

Cotton sweaters are breathable, lightweight, and perfect for transitional weather or layering indoors. They’re soft on the skin and great for those who find wool too itchy. Cotton doesn’t retain as much heat as wool, so it’s best suited for milder climates or casual settings. Expect easy care—most cotton sweaters are machine washable.

Blended fabrics combine the best of both worlds. For example, wool-cashmere blends deliver the softness of cashmere with the durability of wool, while wool-cotton blends offer a balance of warmth and breathability. These blends are often more affordable and easier to care for than pure fibers.

Alpaca wool is soft, silky, and hypoallergenic—great for those with sensitive skin. It’s warmer than regular wool but feels lighter, making it perfect for chilly days without feeling too heavy. Alpaca sweaters often have a natural luster, giving them a polished, luxurious look.

The best sweaters for men should strike the perfect balance—tailored enough to look polished, but comfortable enough for all-day wear. Pay attention to the shoulder and chest areas, which should be roomy enough for an undershirt or a button-down shirt underneath, but also not too loose and still snug and slim enough for looking elevated during standalone wear. Sleeves should hit at the wrist bone when your arms are relaxed at your sides and the overall silhouette should be neither too tight nor too loose. A well-fitting sweater not only enhances your style but also maximizes comfort and complements your body shape.

Opt for designs that work across settings, whether it’s a classic crewneck for casual days, a half-zip for sporty outings, or a cable-knit for a dressier touch. A great sweater should transition with no problem from every location to the next.

Between Style Director Christian Gollayan, who’s spent the past decade covering men’s fashion, and me, who’s tested sweaters, jackets, and everything in between over the past five years, we’ve worn enough knits to fill an entire coat check. Together, we pulled on dozens of sweaters in every fit, fabric, and price point to see which ones actually live up to the hype. We wore them to the office, out to dinner, on weekend errands, and through too many cold commutes. We paid close attention to how each sweater fit (flattering or frumpy?), how it felt against the skin (buttery soft or scratchy mess?), how it held up after a wash, and whether it layered neatly without bulk. After plenty of wear, tear, and mirror checks, we narrowed it down to the sweaters that truly earn their keep—sharp, comfortable, durable, and ready for anything winter throws your way.

The key lies in understanding the different styles of sweaters and pairing them accordingly for various occasions. For a casual, laid-back look that you can wear every day, try a classic crewneck sweater with your go-to pants—perfect for running errands or grabbing coffee with friends. V-neck sweaters are ideal for smart-casual or business-casual settings, whether you're at the office or at dinner, since they layer beautifully over collared shirts. (Zip sweaters also work as such, by the way.)

Cardigan sweaters are easy to dress up: layer a button-down shirt beneath a well-fitted cardigan for a sophisticated, professional-looking appearance, or pair them with khakis and tailored trousers to achieve a preppy look. Similarly, turtlenecks exude refinement and work for cocktail and business-casual attire, easily paired with tailored trousers and blazers for a polished, upscale look. For a more rugged, outdoorsy vibe, opt for a chunky cable knit or fisherman sweater.
